_source: L19 (work plan 2). More of the original's voice, never contradicting it and never a floor count. Built on its own phrases: the Chief's Hall inscription (MEASURE THE GRAIN. COUNT THE FLASKS. KEEP THE DOOR.), the architect and his toys, the bell with no clapper, the scar that misfires every spell, the dungeon still being built. Budget (origins.json): one 'tell' per delve, on its first floor.

The ledger is opened and the figures are made to agree.
A tally is cut into the post. The knife is wiped on a sleeve.
The ale-wife sets out the mugs before she is asked.
Somebody hums, badly, and is left to it.
Wet footprints cross the hall to the hearth and stop there.
The healer counts heads and finds the count is right. She sits down.
The torches are swapped for fresh ones. The old ones are kept for kindling.
Mud is scraped from boots on the iron bar by the door.
The ale-wife counts the heads at the table and sets one more bowl.
The gate-ward lifts the bar without a word and lets the cold in.
A bandage is rolled and tied off. The roll is neat.
The rope is coiled and hung on its peg, as it should be.
Someone puts the kettle on. It is the only cheering anyone does.
The wounded are laid on the long bench. The healer is already there.
Someone sweeps the grit from the doorstep. It comes back with the next boots.
The lamp is trimmed and set on the sill, so the lane can see it.
A pot of broth goes round the table. Nobody asks for the story yet.
The gate-ward writes the number in the book and shuts it.
Boots come off by the hearth. The steam rises off them for an hour.
The stove is fed. The room warms slowly.
Muddy boots line the wall. The floor will be mopped in the morning.
A needle goes through torn leather. The stitches are small and even.
The tally-board is chalked and the chalk put back in its dish.
Somebody hangs the wet cloaks over the rail. The drip is steady.
The gate-ward bars the door and lets the lamp burn on.
The water-bucket goes round. It comes back empty.
Somebody scrapes the mud off the stair with a flat stone.
The lamp is trimmed. It will be wanted again soon enough.
A pot of barley goes on. Nobody asks for it. It is eaten.
The door-ward counts the heads and finds the count right.
Wet wool steams by the fire. Nobody moves it.
The tally is read out loud, once, and then chalked.
Somebody sets a kettle on the coals. It sings before anyone sits.
The gate-ward unbars the door and lets the cold in with them.
Straw is shaken out on the flags. The boots go over it.
The cart is backed to the gate and the sacks counted down.
Bandages are rolled and put back in the chest, the clean ones first.
The stair is swept. Somebody has left a bucket by the foot of it.
A wet cloak is hung to dry and nobody sits near it.
The healer counts the bandages and finds enough.
Bread is torn and passed along the bench, heel last.
The ward lays the bar back across the door and rests a hand on it.
Boots come off at the hearth. The fire is built up without being asked.
Mud is scraped from the boots at the step. The step is swept after.
The kettle goes on before the packs come off.
A lamp is left in the window until the last of them is in.
The chandler counts the stubs and writes down what was burned.
Somebody finds a clean cloth for the blade and says nothing.
The ward sits on the well-edge a while with the lamp between their feet.
The first one in sits on the step and unlaces slowly.
Water is heated before anyone asks for it.
The tally of packs matches the tally that left.
A bed is made up in the back room before it is needed.
The lamp-boy counts the burned wicks back into the tray.
The bell is rung once, and not for alarm.
The ostler has the mules watered before the first one reaches the yard.
The healer sets out her basin and does not ask who is hurt.
Someone hangs the wet cloaks by the stove in order of size.
The ward strikes the day off the gate post and chalks the next.
A pot of barley goes on the fire. It was always going to.
The cooper keeps back a cask for the evening and says nothing of why.
The bell-ringer sits with the rope in his lap and does not pull it.
The guild clerk opens the book to the right page and waits.
The washerwoman wrings out a sleeve and says the water was ready an hour ago.
The gatewarden strikes the hour from the ledger and writes the return beside it.
Somebody has kept the good bench by the fire. It is not the first time.
The ropewright lets the line slack and coils it without a word.
The baker sets out the heel of the loaf. The rest was for the others.
A child runs ahead to the guild door and holds it open.
The lamp-seller looks at the wicks they bring back and nods once.
The old guard has the kettle on. He says it was on anyway.
The cooper rolls a barrel aside to clear the way back in.
The tinker has already put the kettle by the door.
The bellringer gives it one stroke. Just the one.
The fishwife saves the better half of the catch and says it was going spare.
A boy runs to tell the miller's wife. She is already coming.
The ostler has the horse watered and waiting, as though it were any day.
Somebody has swept the stair clear of ash. Nobody owns up to it.
The widow at the corner house opens her shutters again.
The cartwright nods from his doorway and goes back to the wheel.
The chandler counts the stubs in the returned lamps and writes the number down.
The gatewarden strikes the hour out of his ledger, neatly.
The tavern has a stool kept by the fire. It does not say for whom.
The cellar door stands open and nothing came out of it.
The watch stood down early. Nobody argued.
Children play near the stair-head again. Their mothers let them.
The bell rang once and was not followed by another.
Dust on the lintel. The first dust in a long while.
The smith banked the fire and slept through the night.
Lanterns lit, wicks trimmed, shutters left wide.
Supper was loud. Somebody said it first. It was quiet outside.
The bell was rung twice and the second was a happy one.
Wash on the line again. Nobody asked it to be brought in.
The baker made the long loaves. There is somebody to feed.
A cart rolled in with the evening and nobody checked behind it.
The cooper went back to hammering. The sound was welcome.
Somebody opened the shutters on the stair-side of the house.
The well-rope was left slack overnight. Nobody minded.
Dogs slept in the road. Carts went round.
The ostler loosened the straps and let out a breath.
Somebody put the kettle on at the head of the stair.
The smith picked his hammer back up. It was warm yet.
Bread was set out on the step. Nobody asked who for.
The lamp-seller sold out by noon.
A child counted the heroes back up the stair. All there.
The ferryman cast off again. The tide waits for no one, he said.
Shutters came open all down the lane.
The innkeeper counted the bowls and put one away.
The dog was at the stair-head before the first boot showed.
The baker's boy had saved the crust. It was still warm.
Somebody rang the hour at last.
The smith took the dented blade without a word and went to the forge.
The well-woman filled the flasks again. Same price: none.
Doors stood open down the lane till late.
The gate-warden wrote the hour in the book and the number of them. The same number.
A kettle went on in every house on the row.
The step was swept again. Nobody asked who had done it.

lord_intros.hollow_king: The braziers in the hall burn blue, and then burn cold.
lord_intros.grubmother: The floor is wet, and getting wetter.
lord_intros.rattling_host: Somewhere ahead, something counts its own bones out loud.
lord_intros.nightwing: Every torch on the floor gutters at once.
lord_intros.gravewyrm: The dungeon was built around this, and it knows it.
lord_intros.ossuary_lord: It has waited a very long time. A little longer is nothing.
lord_intros.pale_duchess: A lady laughs somewhere ahead, very politely.
lord_intros.mourncoil: Breath steams. Then the steam freezes.

unique_intros.mother_silk: The threads across the doorway are new.
unique_intros.weeping_bowman: A string twangs in the dark, and something weeps after it.
unique_intros.cinderjack: Someone has been playing with the firepits.
unique_intros.kept: A voice the guild knew calls a name the guild remembers.

lord_intros_alt._note: C-cycle 8. Extra intro lines for the SAME eight lords - no new lords. Pick at random from [lord_intros[key]] + lord_intros_alt[key] so a second sighting on one stream does not read identically.
hollow_king: Blue light under the door, and no heat in it.
Something cold is already seated in the hall.
The braziers lean towards whatever just walked in.
The hall is colder at the far end than at the door.
A crown's worth of blue light, and nothing wearing it yet.
The fires burn and give nothing back.
The ash on the floor stands up at the edges.
The far brazier lights itself, and lights blue.
Nothing in this hall is warm, and nothing will be.
The heat leaves the room before anyone does.
A throne you did not see is being sat in.
Something seated takes the room's warmth for itself.
grubmother: The wet reaches the boots before the sound does.
The walls move, and it is not the walls.
Something is birthing in the dark ahead, and not stopping.
The floor gives under the boot and does not spring back.
Something ahead is full and still feeding.
The wet is warm. That is the worst of it.
Something in the dark is laying, and not finished.
The wet in the room has a heartbeat under it.
Ahead of the lamp, the floor is swallowing.
The walls weep, and the weep is thick.
Every crack in the stone is wet and widening.
The room exhales once, and the exhale is warm.
rattling_host: A hundred small knocks, all keeping time.
The dark ahead has too many elbows.
It counts up, and it never reaches an end.
A great many small bones, all in a hurry.
Something ahead is taking stock of itself.
The count carries down the corridor, and it is rising.
Bones against bones, all of them on cue.
The dark ahead keeps roll, and the roll is long.
A cadence of knuckles against stone, coming closer.
Everything upright in that corridor is dead and knows it.
A dry parade is forming between the lamps.
Something calls the rank, and the rank answers.
nightwing: A draught from the ceiling, and the ceiling has wings.
The torches lie flat and stay flat.
Something crosses the lamp twice before you look up.
The lamps duck all together, as if something passed over.
The ceiling is closer than it was, and breathing.
Two shadows for every one thing above you.
The lamp ducks, and the lamp knows why.
Something above the door takes its weight off.
The draught comes in and brings a shape with it.
The lamps all flinch towards the floor at once.
A shadow passes over the party twice in one breath.
The ceiling is lower, suddenly, and has eyes.
gravewyrm: The corridor ahead is a throat.
The stone trembles in long, patient breaths.
Older than the guild, older than the scar - and still hungry.
The walls were cut to let this thing pass, a long age ago.
The floor lifts, very slightly, and settles.
This was never a dungeon. It was a den.
The stone leans in on both sides, hungry.
Older than the floor itself, and awake again.
The corridor narrows because something is filling it.
A low, slow sound - the dungeon itself eating.
The walls flex once and are still again.
This was the first thing. Everything else came after.
ossuary_lord: The bones on the floor are getting up in order.
It does not hurry. It has never had to.
Somewhere ahead, a hand is arranging the dead.
The dead ahead are sorting themselves into ranks.
A dry sound of stacking, somewhere past the lamp.
The dead are being stacked, not dropped.
Somebody down here keeps the books of the dead.
The bones in the alcoves are facing the same way now.
Order, in the dark, and the order is dead.
A ledger is being kept, and the ink is dark.
Something makes the dead stand straight.
pale_duchess: She is already holding the room. You are late.
Someone apologises, sweetly, for what comes next.
The air ahead is warmer, and scented, and wrong.
Somebody is being gracious at you out of the dark.
She has had the room swept for your arrival.
Someone curtseys, in the dark, to nobody.
The air ahead smells of silk and iron.
She has sent word. The word is your name.
Candles down here, and candles cost money.
Somebody polite is putting on gloves.
The hallway ahead has been prepared.
mourncoil: Breath hangs in the air and does not move on.
Frost climbs the walls towards you.
The lamp's own heat gives up first.
Ice on the steel before the first blow.
The cold comes in coils, and tightens.
Ice gathers on the edges of the lamp.
Breath goes out white and does not thin.
The floor cracks underfoot, and the crack is thin.
The lamp's wick stiffens with frost.
Winter arrives in one room, ahead of its season.
The cold steadies, coils, and begins.

unique_intros_alt._note: C-cycle 8. Extra intro lines for the SAME five rare uniques. Same pick rule as lord_intros_alt.
gnawbone: Something is eating the wall, and gaining.
Teeth on stone, all the way down the corridor.
The squeal comes from inside the masonry.
Mortar dust on the floor, and more of it every heartbeat.
There is a hole in that wall that was not there, and it is widening.
Grit on the boots - fresh. The wall is giving it up.
Something grinds down the length of the corridor.
A tooth, white and clean, on the floor. And another.
The wall is softer at the middle than at the ends.
Something in the stone is still eating.
Dust comes off the wall in a steady breath.
mother_silk: The doorway has been re-strung since this morning.
Everything in this room is wrapped and waiting.
Threads tug at the lamp before you touch them.
The lamp catches a thousand threads, all of them new.
Something tidied this room and left the bundles upright.
The silk goes taut, somewhere behind you.
The lamp catches a thread that was not there a step ago.
Something upright on the far wall is wrapped and ready.
The threads in the corner twitch when nothing moves them.
The silk across the doorway is dry. The silk past it is wet.
A line tightens across the back of your neck.
weeping_bowman: A bowstring, then a sob, then nothing.
An arrow in the doorframe, still humming.
He is sorry already, and he will shoot anyway.
A notch, a breath, a sob. In that order.
He aims through tears and does not miss for them.
Grief, and a very good bow.
A string is tested, and the test is sorry.
Arrow-points along the wall, all at the same height.
Someone ahead is loading a bow and asking forgiveness.
A sob, a draw, a snap. In that order, always.
He apologises to the arrows before he lets them go.
Grief draws straight. The shot will land.
cinderjack: Every firepit on the floor is lit, and lit wrong.
Footprints burnt into the stone, going both ways.
Something laughs, and the flames laugh along.
Ash footprints, and the ash is warm.
Every lamp on the floor burns green for a moment.
Something is laughing in the firepit, and the firepit agrees.
Every candle on the floor is lit, and bending wrong.
The firepit ahead is already warm, and nobody is there.
Ash in the lamp - fresh, not old.
Something laughs through a mouth of fire.
Footprints of soot, going two ways.
The fire down here has an opinion.
kept: The guild wrote this name down as lost. It is not lost.
A familiar voice, saying a familiar name, wrongly.
Somebody the roll calls dead calls the roll.
The roll says this one is dead. The roll is wrong, or the voice is.
It wears a guild cloak and remembers the words.
Somebody the guild buried is calling the muster.
A voice from the muster rolls, calling off the muster rolls.
Someone the chapel named is naming the chapel.
The oath is being sung back, in the wrong order.
The dead on the guild board are reading the board.
A cloak the guild buried is walking in it.
Someone the roll gave up calls your name first.

enter: Lamps, steel, door. In that order.
Chalk the corner. Always chalk the corner.
'The door is kept. Say it back to me.'
'Breathe now - we will be busy later.'
'Nobody dies in the first room. It is rude.'
Scratch the turns as we take them.
Count the lamps before the lamps count us.
Chalk the turn before you take it.
Flasks on the right hip, honest side.
If the stair breathes, let it finish.
In. The guild knows where we are.
Mind the bell. Mind what rings it.
Chalk the wall. Trust the chalk.
The stair's behind us. Pretend it isn't.
Slow is how we come back.
Mind the first step. It's always the liar.
Whatever's below, it's heard the bell.
Hands where I can see them. Steel where it can't.
Down we go, and out we come.
Whatever's down there, it's late for us.
Count heads. Then count them again.
Stay close, stay loud, stay alive.
One door. One way. One more time.
Into the scar, and out the other side.
Don't touch the first thing you like.
If it smells of bread, run.
We were never going to stay above ground.
No heroics before the first torch.
Count them in. Count them out.
Chalk the wall as we go.
Slow and quiet, and then slower.
Door behind us. Keep it that way.
Mind the first step. It's always the first.
I've got a good feeling. Don't ask why.
Quick and careful. In that order.
Mind your elbows in the narrows.
We are expected home by dark.
Bring the lamp, not the nerves.
Hands where I can see them.
Fill the lamp before you need it.
Mind the first step. It's loose.
Boots dry now. Not for long.
Hand on the rail. Rail's cold.
Tighten the buckle. Then the other.
Mind the drip on the left.
Mud on the third stair. Slick.
Tie off the pack. It rattles.
Boots dry? Won't be for long.
Hang the lamp where I can see it.
Cold in here. Good. Stays fresh.
Check the rope. Then check it again.
Stay in the file. No wandering.
Count heads at the first landing.
Slow down. The stair is uneven.
Chalk on the wall. Not ours.
Hand on the rail going down.
Steps are worn in the middle.
Keep the torch off the rope.
Count the stairs. Count them back.
Draught on my neck. Behind us?
One at a time through the gap.
Door's stiff. Someone's been behind it.
Lamp low. Let them come to us.
Stairs end here. So does the easy part.
Cold air from the left. Take the right.
Quiet, this one. I don't care for it.
Chalk marks on the wall. Not ours.
Rope tied off. Check the knot.
Dust is thin by the door. Someone's been through.
Keep the torch out of the draught.
Say the plan once. Then no talking.
Boots on the stair. Not ours.
Smell of wet ash. Go slow.
Door was shut from this side.
Floor's dry here. That's not good.
Straw on the flags. Somebody slept.
Cold air from the left. Keep right.
Tally the flasks before we go in.
Chalk mark on the jamb. Someone was here.
Nail in the lintel. Mind the hook.
Smoke on the ceiling. Old fire.
Rope on the floor. Cut, not frayed.
Chalk the wall. Easy way back.
Lamp lit. Door shut behind us.
First step's always the loud one.
Water in the bottle. Water in the boots. Go.
Dark's no worse than last time.
Pace it. We're here a while.
Same stairs as before. Different dark.
Last chance to turn round. Nobody takes it.
Back to the wall until we see.
Whatever is down here, it knows we came.
Same as last time, and last time was fine.
Mind the stair, it is a long one.
Boots on the stair. Eyes up.
The air is stale. That is normal.
Count the doors as we pass.
Dust on the stair. Nobody has been this way.
Old rope on the wall. Do not trust it.
Floor's dry. Let us keep it that way.
Smell of tallow. Someone was here.
Cold air. Keep your voices down.
Torch up. Eyes on the floor.
Walls are damp. Mind the footing.
Wait for the dark to settle. Then go.
Rope out. Anyone slips, we haul.
Stay in the light. Walk in pairs.
lord: Hold the line, not the ground.
It carries a note. Make it short.
'That is the one the Chronicle names.'
'Let it be noted that I came anyway.'
Watch its feet, not its face.
It wants the door. Do not give it.
'It has one good trick. Make it use it.'
'If I fall, somebody finish the sentence.'
It's slow. Be slower than nothing.
This is what we came for.
That's the one from the tell.
Two on it, rest watch the room.
Hold the line, hold the door.
Make it come through the gap.
Last push or last stand - pick!
That one was in the tell. Two of them.
Keep it off the door and off the healer.
It wants the middle - give it the wall.
Hit the wounded side and keep hitting.
Don't trade blows. Make it trade for them.
If it looks at the lamp, the lamp goes out.
Breathe out when it breathes in.
No last stand on floor one, friends.
Spread out. It can't eat everyone.
Eyes on the crown, feet on the floor.
Keep it turning. Keep it turning!
Don't look it in the eye. Look at the knee.
Mind its reach, not its roar.
That's no wandering beast. That's the floor's landlord.
Big. Slow. Ugly. Good, we're prepared.
Break its guard, not your own.
That's the one the stories name.
On my mark, all at once.
It has a pattern. Find the pattern.
Cover the flanks, I've got the front.
Stop looking at the crown, look at the feet.
Eyes up, shields up, mouths shut.
We came for this. Finish it.
Don't let it breathe. Don't let it sing.
It's just a lord. Lords bleed.
Tell the Ford we've got company.
The Ford is counting on us.
Get the healer behind the line!
Names on the roll, lads. Make them count.
Behind the shield, all of you.
Down it goes, same as the rest.
Hold the door. We hold the door.
It's the big one. Hold your ground!
Wait for the tell, then hit.
It bleeds. That's all I need.
Don't look at the crown. Look at the feet.
Make it count. We won't get two.
Stay off the thing's left side!
For the guild, and the grain!
That is the big one. Mind it.
Feet, not face. Feet, not face.
One at a time, and all together.
Watch its shoulder. It moves first.
It's looking at the lamp. Move the lamp.
Do not stand in its line.
Two on the flank. One in front.
One word at a time. Listen for mine.
Mend the one who's hurt first.
It's only one thing. We're five.
Don't look at the eyes. Look at the hands.
It's slow on the turn. Use that.
Shields up. Wait for the swing.
Don't chase it. Let it come.
It's tiring. So are we. Last longer.
Hold your ground. It tires first.
Watch the shoulders. They tell you.
It won't stop. We'll have to.
Count its swings. Then count ours.
Let it spend itself on the shield.
Tank holds. The rest of us work.
Hold the door. Nobody backs out.
Eyes on its feet, not its face.
We've drilled for this. Do it again.
Don't run. It's quicker than you.
Spread out. It can only hit one.
Watch the arm. The arm, not the head.
Count the swings. Then go in.
Stand. That's all it asks of us.
Keep the line. Keep the line.
It's slow to turn. Use that.
One at a time on its left.
Hold. Wait for it to swing.
Keep the healer behind the post.
Hit the leg. Then the leg again.
It looks at the big one. Good.
Steady. It wants us to rush.
Count its swings. Three. Then in.
Mind the floor near its feet.
Look at the feet, not the face.
Shields up. Let it swing itself out.
Don't both stand in one place.
Wait for the breath. Then go.
Keep your back to the wall.
Watch the hands, not the horns.
Spread out. It can't hit three.
One at a time on the left.
Mend the line. Hold the line.
Back off when it breathes in.
Hit and step back. Hit and step back.
Nobody ever won by running first.
Don't look at its hands. Look at its feet.
One of us it will not forget.
Back to the wall. Let it come.
Count its swings. Eight, then step in.
That's the one the town fears.
It wants us to run. Don't.
Take the left. I'll take the weight.
All of it for this one.
Spread out, he cannot hit us all.
I have seen this one on the board.
Lord or no lord, he bleeds.
Stand where he is not looking.
I have seen bigger. Not many.
Hold the door, the rest of you.
He has a long reach. Keep wide.
He is bigger than the stories.
Hold the door. We hold it.
Do not look at his hands.
One at a time. Then all at once.
That is not a door. That is a mouth.
That is no common thing. Mind your feet.
Stand together. It is bigger than it looks.
Steady. Do not look at its hands.
Do not look at the crown.
He has been waiting a long time.
Count the exits. Then forget them.
It has heard us. Hold the line.
Do not look at the crown. Look at the feet.
One at a time. Let it come.
Mind the door behind us. Keep it clear.
Whatever comes next, we came to do it.
trap: Stand clear - I will tread it.
'That was a floor a moment ago.'
'The guild should chalk these. The guild should pay me to chalk these.'
Somebody counted these steps before us.
'Hold still and let me be clever.'
'The stone moved. Stone should not move.'
'That is a pit with a lid on it.'
There's a seam in the stone.
Hands where I can see them.
The architect oils these. Step wide.
Count the tiles. One is counting back.
If it clicks twice, go flat.
Chalk a cross and nobody steps on the cross.
That seam ends in a hinge. Hinges swing.
The weight plate takes less than you think.
Nothing in a corridor is just a corridor.
Tripwire. Thin as a hair, mean as a debt.
Dust on the dart-holes. Fresh dust.
The floor sounds hollow. Because it is.
That's a pit with a rug on it.
Scorch marks. Somebody learned the hard way.
A smooth stone in a rough wall. Nope.
Watch the lintel. Watch the lintel!
If it's too clean, it's bait.
Third tile, left. Stay off it.
Something clicked. Tell me it was you.
Dust on the floor, but not on that stone.
The wall is too clean. Step back.
Smell that? Oil. Don't strike a flint.
Floor sings when you step. Stop stepping.
The chalk turns red where it bites.
I hate floors. Name one honest floor.
Who left a floor that does that?
Dust on the stone, no dust on the plate.
Plate under my foot. Don't move.
Too clean a floor. Too clean.
Hinge is oiled. Who oils a hinge in here?
Fresh oil on a rusted hinge.
Pass me the chalk. Mark that tile.
Scratches on the floor. Follow them.
Tap it with the pole first.
Dust is disturbed. Not by us.
That plate is newer than the rest.
Spare me the heroics. Go round.
Gap in the dust. Step over.
I'll go first. Mind my rope.
That's a pit. Smells of it.
Feel the draught? Vent in the wall.
Slow. Test it with the pole.
Half a bolt in the post. Somebody missed.
Hold the lamp lower. Look at the seams.
Two stones don't match. Mind them.
Spent a dart. Found it in my boot.
Old bones by the door. Why?
Stand back. I'll throw a stone.
Crack in the ceiling. Dust falling.
Sand on the step. Hiding something.
Thread across the doorway. Mind it.
Smell of oil. Something's wound tight.
A hole in the wall at knee height.
Latch is too clean. Leave it.
Pebbles on the step. Don't kick them.
Wire at the ankle. Down low.
Third stair is shallow. Skip it.
Draught from the floor. A vent.
Bone dust on the step. Back up.
Ceiling is lower here. Mind your head.
Twine across the door. Cut it from the side.
Dust is thinner there. Step round.
Wire at the ankle. Lift your foot.
Slab rocks. Weight on the rim.
Hinge oil, fresh. Somebody maintains this.
Grit falling from above. Hold still.
Spike holes in the floor. Count them.
Wire at the ankle. Step over.
Fresh oil on the hinge. Not ours.
Wall's scratched at knee height. Mind it.
Floor's polished here. Wrong kind of polished.
Dry bones in a pile. Something put them there.
Rope across the way. Too tidy.
Smells of oil and old iron.
Plate by the door. Step round.
Dust on everything but this one tile.
Hold the lamp out. Look first.
Old oil on the hinge. Not so old.
Pitch on the wall. Fire trap, likely.
Someone set this to be found.

epitaphs: Measured the grain. Counted the flasks. Kept the door.
The scar keeps what it takes.
Went down with a lamp. Did not come up.
The guild writes the name and keeps it.
Somewhere below, a bell with no clapper rings once.
One floor too many.
Lit a lamp. The dark kept it.
Counted every flask but the last.
The guild writes the name; the scar keeps the rest.
Measured the grain. The grain ran out.
Went down proving something. Proved it.
Kept the door, until the door kept them.
The bell with no clapper rang, and they did not come up.
Named on the roll, and marked with a dagger.
Paid the guild's price in full.
The door held. They did not.
Last seen going down, lamp high.
The Chronicle spells the name right, at least.
Fed the scar and asked for nothing.
A good hand with a flask, to the end.
Kept the door one floor too long.
Took the stair down and the guild's coin with it.
Knew the shapes. Met a new one.
Walked in light, left in the dark.
The lamp came back. They did not.
Marked present on the roll, and absent everywhere else.
Trimmed the lamp low to save oil. Saved oil.
Bellmire remembers the name and nothing else.
Went down for the gold and found the rest of it.
Mended everyone but themselves.
The flask was full. The hand was slow.
Stood where the floor lied.
No body to bury. The guild buried the name.
Measured the grain. Did not measure the dark.
Kept the door. Lost the room.
The lamp was lit. That is something.
Brought everyone else up.
Went down for a friend. Stayed with them.
Never once short on flasks.
The guild's ledger is square. The rest is not.
Came up as a name on a list.
Knew better and went anyway.
Stood where the lord swung.
Spent the last flask on somebody else.
The dark took the lamp, the coat and the rest.
Counted the flasks for the whole band.
Bought the stair with their own back.
Answered the crier. Did not answer the roll.
Died rich, two floors from the surface.
Held the stair while the others climbed.
No last words. Plenty of warning.
The scar misfired, and so did the luck.
Mended the door, if not the hand.
Last of the lamp oil, first into the room.
Marked with a dagger on the Guild Roll.
The flask was empty and the hand was steady.
Took the deep road for the guild's coin.
The bell with no clapper kept its silence.
Kept the door until the door went.
Measured twice. The dark measured once.
Carried the lamp for everyone else.
Paid the ferryman early.
Went in first. Always went in first.
The band came up. Not all of it.
Named on the roll, and the roll is kept.
Stood where standing was the whole job.
Last flask given away, and gladly.
Brave, loud, and brief.
The scar took a good one.
Walked down smiling. Bellmire remembers that much.
Spent every copper on the right things.
Nothing left behind but the chalk marks.
Fell on a floor nobody has a name for.
Counted the flasks. There were none left to count.
Kept the lamp lit for the ones behind.
Measured the grain and never the risk.
Walked back up in somebody else's story.
The flasks were counted. The luck was not.
Went down for one more room.
Last through the door, as always.
Knew the floor lied and stood on it anyway.
Bought the band an hour.
Took the blow meant for the mender.
The guild's coin outlived the hand that took it.
Chalked the way back for everybody else.
Never once left the door open.
Short on flasks, long on nerve.
The lamp burned down to nothing, and so did they.
Counted out, called up, never came.
Spent on the scar, like the rest of it.
Fought where the ground was worst.
Left the roll a dagger and the band a chance.
Found what the gold was buried under.
The quiet took them before the Chronicle did.
Stayed to hold what everyone else had let go.
Bellmire measures the grain. The scar measured them.
Kept the door. The door did not keep them.
Went down rich in flasks and came back in the Chronicle.
Stood where the lamp was. That was the whole plan.
Named in the roll, missed at the gate.
Measured the grain for a town that outlived them.
The scar misfired. So did the luck.
Last through the door, always.
Spent their last flask on somebody else.
A good shield. A bad floor.
Took the front rank and kept it.
Their lamp came up. They did not.
Fought one room past sense.
The guild writes it; the scar keeps it.
Died owed wages. Bellmire paid them anyway.
Carried two out. Could not carry themselves.
Asked for the hard corner and got it.
The bell with no clapper rang for them, in the way it does.
Went looking for a name and found one.
Held the stair while the roll climbed it.
Laughed at the tell. The tell was right.
Counted wrong once.
Steady hands, short night.
Never once stepped where they were told not to.
The dark took the lamp first, then the rest.
Paid for the hall's roof in a single delve.
Chalked the wall, walked the room, stayed in it.
A quiet fighter and a loud end.
Said they would be back by the bell.
Wore the guild's colours all the way down.
Out of flasks, out of floor, out of time.
The scar does not haggle.
Bellmire keeps the name. That is the deal.
Kept the door until the door gave.
Chalked the way out. Took the way in.
Went down for the tenth and paid the whole.
The lamp was found. Nothing else was.
Counted the grain, measured the flasks, mixed the two.
Last of the party to run. First on the stone.
Argued with the scar. Lost on points.
Died rich, two rooms short of the stair.
Owed the guild nothing. The guild owed them more.
Stood exactly where they were told. It was the wrong place.
Brave, and only once.
A good hand with a lamp.
Found the trap. Found it properly.
Went in loud. Came out quiet.
Named on this stone and nowhere else.
Took the lord's eye. The lord took the rest.
The flask was empty. So was the room.
Carried two out and went back for the third.
Never once asked what was below.
Fought in the dark without a word.
Oiled every hinge on the way down.
Short of the stair by a long way.
The scar collects. This was an instalment.
Buried in Bellmire, which is more than most are offered.
Knew the tell. Went anyway.
Spent their last coin on brews for somebody else.
Good shield. Better friend.
Walked the room twice. The second time was one too many.
The dark learned their name.
Held the gap. The gap held.
Paid for the bell. It still has no clapper.
Went down counting, and reached a number nobody will say.
Kept the door. The door kept back.
Measured well. Spent well. Spent last.
Walked the room three times. Nobody saw the third.
Paid the tenth. Paid the rest.
Named in the honest hand.
The scar wrote their name last, and underlined it.
Oil enough. Luck short.
Chalk on the lintel. None on the way out.
Went for a friend. The friend came back.
Last flask spent on somebody else's wound.
Held the gap one breath too long.
The guild's tenth, paid in full.
Knew the tell. The tell knew them.
Counted the grain. Was the last grain counted.
A good shield, kept by a better one.
Went down singing. The dark learned the tune.
The lamps they lit are still lit.
Carried the standard. Carried it down.
Rang the bell with no clapper, and was answered.
Spent well, and the guild rounds up.
Their chalk mark is on three floors and none above.
Lantern full. Flask full. Cup empty.
Paid in oil, in iron, in last.
The architect's toys took a thumb. Then the hand.
Went where the map had an edge.
Second breath, first door, last room.
Walked in behind the lamp and did not walk out behind it.
The stone remembers a name the guild has not written yet.
Stood between the party and it, and stood.
Weighed their tenth with honest hands.
The dark is quieter where they fell.
Carried water down. Carried nothing up.
Their flask is still corked, on a floor the guild has not named.
A reeve's son. A guild's man. A scar's take.
The chalk at the stair says they went. The hand is theirs.
Spent the last roll on a stranger.
The door they kept is still kept.
No bell rang. The dark did not need to be told.
They counted to the number, and to one more.
The guild writes their name small, and underlines it twice.
Kept watch. The watch kept.
Paid the tenth in blood.
Measured honest. Spent short.
The scar heard the name twice.
Lamp, flask, door - all three ran out.
Walked a lord off its feet. Did not walk back.
Chalked the turn and took it anyway.
A good hand at the bucket. A worse day on the stair.
Held the gap, closed the gap, stayed in it.
Fell forward. The guild rounds up.
The dark was owed. The dark collected.
Lit a lamp against a greater one.
Bellmire owes them a stone it cannot read.
Spent the last chalk on the last turn.
Trimmed the wick. The wick outlived them.
Counted the band and came up short of themselves.
The door is kept. The keeper is not.
Took one for the stair.
Steady at the oil. Steady to the end.
Came up in the ledger, not in daylight.
Measured the floor. The floor measured back.
Carried the lamp down. Nobody carried it up.
Honest brew, honest wages, dishonest floor.
Fought the shape, not the number.
Died owed a drink at the apothecary's slate.
Spoke the word. The scar finished the sentence.
The lord took the note they carried.
Walked through smoke for a stranger.
The chalk mark is still there.
Bought the door another breath.
The dark learned to count that high.
Paid for their own name in the Chronicle.
Held where the floor would not.
Stood up twice after they should have fallen.
The scar counted them in, and in again.
First through the door. First on the stone.
Mended until they could not.
The last flask, honestly spent.
Named small. Written large.
Rang the clapperless bell and got an answer.
Counted the flasks, then spent the last.
Kept the door until the door kept them.
Went first so the rest could go second.
The lamp outlived the hand.
Fell where the chalk ends.
Owed nothing. Paid it all.
Measured the grain and the dark, and the dark was bigger.
A good delver. A better friend. A worse sense of floors.
The scar took the name. The Ford takes the rest.
Left a lamp lit at the landing.
Rang no bell, asked no pity.
Held the line one breath too long, and that was the length of it.
Home is up the stair. They did not make the stair.
Trusted the plate. The plate was not trustworthy.
Heroism, briefly.
Died the way the guild hoped they wouldn't.
The last torch, the last step.
Carried the flask for the others. Never opened it.
The wall remembers. The ledger forgets.
Told the dark a joke. It did not laugh.
Mended others until the mending ran out.
Brave on credit, honest to the end.
Fell with the door in sight.
Their boots are still warm at the entrance. They are not.
Name chalked at the post, name wiped by the damp.
Went deeper than the lamp.
Struck once more than the dark allowed.
Buried by the scar, mourned by the Ford.
Left the ledger balanced and the stair unfinished.
Died laughing at a trap, and the trap was funny.
Was told to wait. Did not.
Counted every coin, missed the last stair.
Left a good boot and a better joke.
The bell tolled once for the brave, once for the bold, once for them.
Never saw the third trap.
Mended a hundred, mended none today.
Argued with the dark, and lost the argument.
Died as promised: loudly.
Went down singing. The scar kept the tune.
Fell with a full flask. A waste, said the others.
Owed the tavern two drinks. Paid in full.
Stood between us and the door. Still does.
The Ford remembers a laugh like theirs.
Kept the lamp lit past the last of the oil.
Was brave for a whole minute longer than sense allowed.
Found the thing in the dark, and it found them.
Had a plan. Was not the plan's fault.
The scar took the name and left the hat.
A good hand with a lock, a poor hand with this one.
Rest. The lamp is ours to carry now.
Sold the sword to buy the dawn. Paid in kind.
Went after the lord. The lord was home.
They said it was just a rat. They were right, but large.
Was the quickest of us, until they were not.
Told us not to look back. We looked.
The dark owes them a favour, and has not paid.
Fell where the stair ends. A fitting place.
Left a debt, a dog, and a dozen friends.
They carried the bell, and the bell carried them.
Died before the punchline. We finished it for them.
Planted a flag. The flag stayed.
Never drank the last flask. We did, in their name.
A kind soul in an unkind hole.
Their last words were practical, as ever.
Went out like a candle, and the room was brighter for the burning.
Counted the steps all the way down.
The Ford will tell it wrong. We will tell it right.
Not every blade finds a hand worthy of it. This one did.
Two knees, one oath, no regrets.
Left behind a full ledger and an empty chair.
Held the line one breath too long, and that breath held us.
Tired of the road, rested in the scar.
The last torch was theirs, and they kept it burning.
Marked the way for us in their own blood. Considerate.
The lord laughed. They did not live to hear it stop.
Walked well, fell well, will be missed well.
Paid the toll. It was steeper than advertised.
They went to see what the dark was for.
A name carved late, in a hurry, with love.
Signed the roll in ink. Went down in chalk.
Left the lamp burning for whoever came second.
The crier will say the name once. The stone will say it longer.
Brave on the stair, braver at the bottom, and no further.
A debt to the Ford, paid in full and in person.
Kept faith with the door and nothing else in the dark did.
Mended the party for a hundred paces. The hundred-and-first was the scar's.
Bought a good blade. Died of an average one.
The scar owed them nothing and took them anyway.
Last seen holding the line. The line is still there.
Their lamp went out last. It was not a comfort.
Packed for a week. Needed an hour.
Fell with a joke half told. The party finished it.
No tomb, no stone. A chalk mark by the guild stair will do.
Went down singing so the dark would know the way out.
They asked what was behind the door. Now they know.
The grain was measured. The nerve was not.
A name on the roll, a gap on the bench.
Swore they would be back for supper. Supper kept.
Loved the ale, the Ford, and a bad idea.
Lived loud. Died louder. The mine remembers.
A shield for the weak, a shoulder for the proud.
Trusted the floor. The floor had other plans.
Not a legend. Better: a regular.
Carried the party's flasks and the party's secrets. Dropped neither.
Dug in, held on, and went under with the tide of it.
The marsh would have had them anyway. The scar was quicker.
Cheerful to the last torch.
Left a boot at the stair-head and a ledger squared to the penny.
They said the room was quiet. That is how rooms say yes.
A hero by the roll. A friend by the fire.
Counted the exits. Chose the wrong one with great style.
The guild gave them a bed, a blade, and a number. The scar gave them rest.
Ran the stair twice for a stranger and a third time for nobody.
They are not lost. They are exactly where the dark put them.
Never missed a watch. Missed the last one.
Fell as the lamp-bearer, and the lamp lit the way home.
Do not weep. They would have charged you for it.
Went down to the scar with a laugh and a bad knee.
Ate well, drank well, delved badly.
The crier forgot the name. The stone did not.
Called the roll on the way in. Answered for everyone on the way out. Until once.
Stood between the lord and the lamp-boy. Stands there still.
Kept a tally on the wall. The tally has one more mark now.
A short life with a long reputation.
Their last word was a flask count. It was correct.
They knew the risk, signed for it, and paid it.
Wept for nothing, feared nothing, found the scar anyway.
Left the door kept, the fire banked, and the debt forgiven.
Fell on the stair where the stone is worn by better feet.
The Ford carries their name downstream. Someone will read it.
Best of a bad lot, which is saying something good.
A good death is a bad bargain. They took it twice.
Paid in bits and in blood, and neither was refunded.
Slept on the roll. Woke in the scar.
They went to prove the dark wrong. It stayed right.
There is a candle at the guild post with their name on it, and it is not for show.
Lamp low, nerve high, luck out.
Sold the sword. Kept the shield. Used the shield.
Paid up. Went down. Paid again.
Left the bread on the table for after.
Knew the stair by heart. The stair did not know them.
Cut the rope behind them so no one would follow.
Fixed the hinge. Forgot the latch.
Counted twice. Missed one.
Ate before they went. Good habit.
Wrote home on the way down.
Carried a spare lamp. Did not need the spare.
Said they would be back by supper.
Held the line one breath longer than the line wanted.
Mended their boots. Walked in them.
Had the month's pay in the belt. Spent none of it.
Last to leave every room. Last again.
Taught the new ones where to stand.
Brought the others back. Did not come back themselves.
Never lost a coin. Lost the rest.
Quiet in the tavern. Quiet now.
Paid the ferryman twice.
Fair with the share. Fair at the end.
No kin. The guild keeps the candle.
Left a good cloak on the peg.
Knew when to back away. Once did not.
Stood in the doorway so the others could run.
Stayed to see the door shut.
Their dog waited at the gate a week.
Planned for everything but the thing that came.
Thirty good days and one bad one.
Brewed their own flasks. Drank the last one.
Went by the book. The book had a page missing.
Did the dull work well. Nobody wrote it down. We did.
Taken in the second room. Missed in the first.
Afraid the whole way down. Went anyway.
Their ale is still on the slate.
Honest about the odds. Went regardless.
Kept the second torch dry. Never lit it.
Always checked the knots. Once, did not.
Paid in full. Owed nothing. Owed.
Said little. Meant all of it.
Carried the water. Carried it every day.
Never lost a coin of the guild's.
Went down singing under their breath.
Left the lamp where the next one would find it.
Held the rope for three. Let go for none.
Had a good laugh and a poor sense of direction.
Sold their last spare boots to buy a better sword.
Knew every tavern song, and the bad verse too.
Paid the stable boy double. Said it was for luck.
Last words: 'It is only a draught.'
Slept light. Not light enough.
Kept the books straight, even in the dark.
Counted the party in. Counted it out short.
Stood watch on the stair and did not sit down.
Fed the guild cat every morning.
Mended the torch bracket nobody asked about.
Went second. Said it was the safer place.
Wore the dented helm with some pride.
Said the ledge looked sound.
Dropped the key. Went back for it.
Walked in whistling. Out of tune.
Took the long way round, and the short way down.
Owed the smith for a blade. Paid in the only way left.
Wrote home on Fifthday. The letter is still on the sill.
Never missed a roll call until the one.
Had the steadiest hands in the Hall.
Brought the good bread for everyone.
Went back for a friend. Both are on the stone.
Bit of a fool. All of a friend.
Argued with the map and lost.
Held a wall of strangers once. Nobody remembers the face.
Did the work. Asked for the pay after.
Trusted the rope.
Kept the torch dry through three floods.
Taught half the guild to tie a knot.
Drank to the dead, then joined them.
The apothecary kept a flask back, in case.
Told the same joke every delve. It was a good joke.
Rang the alarm. Did not hear it stop.
Left a pair of gloves on the guild peg.
Left a half-eaten loaf and a full purse.
Held the door a breath longer than the door deserved.
Slow on the stair, fast when it mattered.
Fell where the lamp last showed them.
Paid up, signed on, went down.
The roll has a gap. Bellmire has noticed.
Stood in the gap. The gap held.
Never met a stair they did not argue with.
Quiet, steady, and missed.
A good hand with a lantern.
Their chair at the guild table stays empty one night.
Went down for the town. The town remembers.
Few words. Fewer complaints.
Early to the gate. Late to nothing.
Ate a hot meal before the stair, as advised.
Counted every flask twice and drank the last of them.
Honest in the dark, which is rarer than it sounds.
Spent the whole wage on the chapel roof.
Buried by the east wall, where the sun comes first.
Their name is on the roll. The roll is kept.
Paid the toll at every landing. Not the last one.
Left the porch lamp lit. It is still lit.
Carried the rope. The rope came back.
Knew every stair by its sound.
Ate before the descent, as advised.
Did the sums twice. The floor did them once.
Mended the strap, and then the strap held.
Four good winters, and one bad stair.
Left a boot at the gate. It is kept for them.
Tied the knots right. It was not the knots.
Asked for the long rope, and was given it.
Said they would be back by the evening bell.
Was owed three coppers at the bakery. Forgiven.
Held the lamp for the others.
Sharpened the blade the night before. Neatly done.
Nobody heard it. Somebody wrote it down.
Weighed the pack, and took less than they could carry.
Had a good name at the tavern, and kept it.
Went first, because someone had to.
Counted the stairs down. Did not need to count up.
The cart is oiled and the stall is kept. Nobody has the heart to let it.
Slept well the last night. That is something.
Their bread is still on the sill.
Brought back the wounded twice. Not a third time.
Wore the old boots for luck. They were good boots.
Left the debts paid and the door unlatched.
Never raised a voice. Never lost a flask.
Down by the second lamp. The lamp is still there.
Read the notices, minded the rules, went down anyway.
Knew the cost. Went.
Paid the ferryman before the ferry. Rowed home anyway.
Mended the net, then the roof, then went down.
Carried the lamp for the others. It was the lighter load.
Said little. Held the line. Held it again.
Taught the youngest to tie a knot. The knot held.
Ate last, slept least, never complained of either.
Left a loaf for the next shift. Somebody ate it.
Kept the books honest. Kept the party honest more.
Turned back once. Went again. Did not turn back twice.
Sharpened the blade at dusk. Did not need it at dawn.
Marked the wrong turns on the wall for those behind.
Went down with a sound back and a clear conscience.
Always first through the door. The door was kind to the rest.
Counted the arrows. There were enough. There were not.
Patched the cloak with her own thread. The cloak outlived her.
Won the toss on the way down. Lost nothing but time.
Knew every step of the stair. It did not matter.
Kept a candle in the pocket for the last dark.
Sold the good boots to feed the town. Wore the old ones down.
Hummed on the stair. The hum stopped. The stair did not.
Was owed two coppers. The town paid them to the grave.
Stood between the wounded and the dark. Then did not stand.
Slept well the night before. That was all there was to ask.
Walked the floors twice. The third was not a walk.
The rope was theirs. The rope came up. They did not.
Died at work. The work was done.
Answered the horn. Always answered the horn.
Said the hour was fair. It was.
Did the small things right. The large ones followed.
Their name is on the board. The board is plain wood.
Kept the count. Kept it to the end.
Paid up. Paid the guild, paid the innkeeper, paid the stair.
Fixed the hinge the day before. It still opens.
Sat the late watch so another could sleep.
No song. The work was the song.
Good with a rope. The rope was good with them.
Left the lamp lit on the landing.
Ate before the stair. Always ate before the stair.
Never late. Not even for this.
Their boots are by the door. Someone has oiled them.
Carried the heavy end without being asked.
Did not boast. There was nothing to boast about, and much to be proud of.
Left a debt of one loaf. It has been paid.
Held the line while the others went up.
Knew every name on the board. Now they are on it.
Dry bread, cold water, level head.
A fair hand with a lantern and a fairer one with a neighbour.
Went down at first light. The light is still on.
Mended the shield, then used it.
Quiet in life, quiet below.
The stair took the last of the day, and them with it.
Swept the guild floor on the morning they left.
Asked for no thanks and got a plain stone.
Their place at the table is kept.
Wrote their own name in a steady hand.
The flask was full. The hand was steady. The floor was not.
Did the work, left the tools clean.
Came for the coin. Stayed for the company.
Honest weight, honest word, honest end.
Mended the roof before the rain, then the rain came.
Ate standing up. Fought the same way.
Hung the cloak on the same peg every night.
