bandit_camps.while: Cut stone and lime go missing; building in town stalls for want of either.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Quarry Camp is emptied out. The stone comes down the road at an honest price.
appears_alt: Old Peck's lot are in the worked-out quarry, selling Bellmire its own stone back.
The old quarry has men in it again, and they are not masons. Old Peck is there.
The stone cart came in empty and expensive. Old Peck holds the quarry.
Old Peck has moved into the quarry and set his own price on what the town already owns.
Old Peck has put a roof on the worked-out quarry and a price on the stone.
Old Peck is back in the quarry, with a cart of stone to sell the town.
Stone is dear in town again. Old Peck has the worked-out quarry.
while_alt: Cut stone and lime go missing; building in town stalls for want of either.
No stone, no lime - whatever Bellmire is raising stops where it stands.
The quarry's take goes to Old Peck. The scaffolds stand idle.
Stone and lime both vanish on the road. Every build in town waits.
Stone and lime stop arriving, and every wall in town stops going up.
Cut stone and lime are sold back dear or not at all; building stalls.
Masons wait on stone Old Peck holds; every build in town slows.
cleared_alt: The Quarry Camp is emptied out. The stone comes down the road at an honest price.
Old Peck is walked out of the quarry. The masons have their stone.
The quarry belongs to the town again - and so does the stone in it.
Old Peck sells nothing further. Building starts where it stopped.
The Quarry Camp is cleared. Old Peck is left with his own hammer and no buyers.
The quarry is emptied of Old Peck's lot. The stone comes at an honest price.
The Quarry Camp is cleared. The masons get their stone and their lime.

bandit_camps.name: The Lampless Road
bandit_camps.appears: Wick Harrow's crew put out the road lamps one by one, and work the dark they made.
bandit_camps.while: Nobody travels after dusk; the night trade stops and the Ford shuts early.
bandit_camps.cleared: The lamps burn the whole length of the road again. Wick Harrow walks it in chains.
appears_alt: Wick Harrow's crew are putting out the road lamps again, and working the dark they make.
Three lamps dark on the road tonight. Wick Harrow is back at it.
The road has gone black a mile at a time. Wick Harrow holds the dark end of it.
Someone is harvesting the lamp oil and the travellers both. Wick Harrow.
The road lamps are going out one by one. Wick Harrow is working his way up the line.
The road lamps are out again, one by one. Wick Harrow is at work.
The road went dark last night. Wick Harrow's crew were seen in it.
while_alt: Nobody travels after dusk; the night trade stops and the Ford shuts early.
The road is dark and empty after sundown - no night trade, and the Ford closes its doors.
Dusk ends the day's trade now. The Ford bolts up early and takes less.
After dark the road belongs to Wick. The night trade is finished and the Ford shuts.
After dusk the road is shut to all comers; the night trade dies and the Ford closes early.
No one risks the road after dusk; the night trade stops and the Ford shuts early.
The Ford shuts early and the night trade dies; nobody travels after dark.
cleared_alt: The lamps burn the whole length of the road again. Wick Harrow walks it in chains.
Every lamp lit, end to end. Wick Harrow is carried past them.
The dark is given back to the sky. The Ford keeps its late hours.
Wick Harrow's crew are out of the dark and into the light of a cell.
Every lamp is lit by morning. Wick Harrow is walked in, in the light.
Every lamp on the road is lit. Wick Harrow is marched home in chains.
The Lampless Road is lit end to end, and Wick Harrow is taken.

bandit_camps.name: The Weir Camp
bandit_camps.appears: Marek Two-Coin has fortified the old weir and charges the river for using itself.
bandit_camps.while: River trade pays twice; the Ford's takings fall while the weir stands.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Weir Camp is broken open. The river runs toll-free again.
appears_alt: Marek Two-Coin has the old weir fortified, and charges the river for using itself.
There are palings on the old weir and Marek Two-Coin behind them.
The barges came up paying twice. Marek Two-Coin holds the weir.
Marek Two-Coin is back on the weir, collecting with both hands.
Marek Two-Coin has bricked up the weir and hung a toll-board on it.
Marek Two-Coin is on the weir again, collecting from the river.
Barges are stopped at the old weir. Marek Two-Coin wants his second coin.
while_alt: River trade pays twice; the Ford's takings fall while the weir stands.
Every barge is charged at the weir first - the Ford takes less for the same traffic.
Marek skims the river before Bellmire does. The Ford's books thin out.
Two tolls on one river. The Ford's share drops while the Weir Camp holds.
Barges pay the weir and then pay the Ford; Bellmire's takings drop while the weir holds.
River trade pays Marek at the weir and then pays the Ford; the Ford's takings fall.
Every barge pays twice; the Ford's takings fall for as long as the weir stands.
cleared_alt: The Weir Camp is broken open. The river runs toll-free again.
Marek Two-Coin is taken off the weir with neither coin. The barges pay once.
The palings come off the weir. The Ford's takings come back.
One toll on the river now, and it is the town's.
The weir is broken, and its toll-board floats off downriver.
The weir is broken open and Marek Two-Coin has lost both coins.
The Weir Camp falls. Barges pass once, and pay once.

bandit_camps.name: The Ashen Barrow
bandit_camps.appears: Grell the Patient has dug into the barrow mound and watches the market road out of it.
bandit_camps.while: Market-bound carts are picked off; stalls stand empty on market day.
bandit_camps.cleared: The barrow is emptied of the living. Grell the Patient stays behind in it.
appears_alt: Grell the Patient has dug into the barrow mound and watches the market road out of it.
There is a hole in the barrow and eyes in the hole. Grell the Patient is waiting.
Grell the Patient is in the Ashen Barrow again, and he can wait longer than the town can.
The market road has a watcher nobody hired. Grell is in the mound.
Grell the Patient has been seen at the barrow's mouth. He is very good at being still.
Grell the Patient is back in the barrow, and has not hurried yet.
A cart was found empty on the market road. Grell is watching from the Barrow.
while_alt: Market-bound carts are picked off; stalls stand empty on market day.
The carts do not arrive. Market day opens half-stalled.
Grell takes them one cart at a time - and the market shows the gaps.
Every cart for market is a cart for Grell. The stalls stand bare.
Market-bound carts are picked off from the mound; stalls stand empty on market day.
Market carts are picked off from the barrow; stalls stand empty on market day.
Grell takes the carts bound for market, one at a time, and the stalls thin out.
cleared_alt: The barrow is emptied of the living. Grell the Patient stays behind in it.
Grell ran out of patience first. The market road carries carts.
The Ashen Barrow is sealed with its proper tenants. Market day fills up.
Grell waits in the barrow permanently now. The stalls are stocked.
The barrow is cleared of everything that breathes. The market road is quiet and honest.
The Barrow is cleared. Grell the Patient is not leaving it.
The Ashen Barrow is quiet. The market carts come through.

bandit_camps.name: The Hollow Stand
bandit_camps.appears: Ivett Crow's archers hold the wood where the road bends, and they do not miss twice.
bandit_camps.while: Couriers and tax carts are lost at the bend; news and coin both arrive late or not at all.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Hollow Stand is cleared. The road bends past nothing worse than trees.
appears_alt: Ivett Crow's archers hold the wood at the road's bend, and they do not miss twice.
The bend has gone quiet. Ivett Crow's bows are in the Hollow Stand.
A courier's horse came in without a courier. Ivett Crow holds the bend.
There are arrows in the bend-post again. The Hollow Stand is manned.
Ivett Crow's archers are in the trees at the bend. Several carts have found this out.
Ivett Crow's archers are in the wood at the bend again.
A courier came in with an arrow through his satchel. The Hollow Stand is held.
while_alt: Couriers and tax carts are lost at the bend; news and coin both arrive late or not at all.
Nothing gets round the bend - the post stops and the tax carts with it.
News ages on the road and the coin never finishes the journey.
The bend eats couriers. Word and money both come late, or not.
Couriers and tax carts are lost at the bend; news and coin arrive late or not at all.
Couriers and tax carts vanish at the bend; news and coin come late or not at all.
The bend in the road takes riders and carts, and Bellmire hears and earns late.
cleared_alt: The Hollow Stand is cleared. The road bends past nothing worse than trees.
Ivett Crow misses once, and once is enough. The post runs.
The wood at the bend is emptied of bowmen. Coin and word arrive on time.
Ivett Crow comes out of the Stand with her string cut. The road is open.
The wood at the bend is cleared. Ivett Crow's bow hangs in the Watch-house.
The Hollow Stand is cleared. Ivett Crow's bows hang in the Watch house.
The road bends past trees and nothing else. The couriers ride.

bandit_camps.name: The Shepherd's Fold
bandit_camps.appears: Dunn Halfhand has taken the high fold and keeps whatever flock he finds in it.
bandit_camps.while: Wool and mutton stop coming down off the hills; the cloth trade and the tavern both feel it.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Fold changes shepherd. Dunn Halfhand leaves with a quarter hand and no flock.
appears_alt: Dunn Halfhand has taken the high fold and keeps whatever flock he finds in it.
The high fold has a shepherd who shears other men's sheep. Dunn Halfhand.
No flock has come down off the hills this week. Dunn Halfhand holds the fold.
Dunn Halfhand is in the Shepherd's Fold, counting a flock he never raised.
Dunn Halfhand has gone up to the high fold, and the flocks have stopped coming down.
Dunn Halfhand has the high fold again and everything grazing in it.
No flocks have come down off the hills. Dunn Halfhand is at the Fold.
while_alt: Wool and mutton stop coming down off the hills; the cloth trade and the tavern both feel it.
No wool, no mutton. The weavers slow and the tavern's pot goes thin.
The hills send nothing down. Cloth gets dear and the tavern serves less.
Dunn keeps the flocks. The cloth trade and the kitchen both run short.
The hill flocks stay on the hill; wool and mutton dry up, and the weavers and the tavern notice.
Wool and mutton stay on the hill; the cloth trade and the tavern feel it.
The hill flocks go to Dunn instead of the market; cloth and the tavern go short.
cleared_alt: The Fold changes shepherd. Dunn Halfhand leaves with a quarter hand and no flock.
Dunn Halfhand is driven off the high fold. The flocks come down.
The fold holds sheep and no thieves. Wool and mutton come in again.
Dunn counts to nine now. The hills send their flocks down.
The high fold is retaken. The flocks come down in a long, relieved line.
The Fold is retaken and Dunn Halfhand is sent down with nothing.
Shepherds return to the Fold. Dunn Halfhand does not.

bandit_camps.name: The Lime Kiln
bandit_camps.appears: Mad Tibb's crew sleep in the lime kiln and come out white as ghosts to work the road.
bandit_camps.while: Lime and mortar never reach the masons; whatever Bellmire is building stops where it stands.
bandit_camps.cleared: The kiln is cold and empty. Mad Tibb is walked back to town the colour of chalk.
appears_alt: Mad Tibb's crew sleep in the lime kiln and come out white as ghosts to work the road.
There are white men on the road at dusk. Mad Tibb is in the kiln again.
The lime cart was taken by something that looked dead and laughed. Mad Tibb.
Mad Tibb has the lime kiln, and the chalk on his crew is not the worst thing on them.
White-faced figures are working the road at dusk. Mad Tibb has the kiln again.
White figures were seen on the road at dusk. Mad Tibb is in the kiln again.
Mad Tibb has the lime kiln and has painted himself for the road.
while_alt: Lime and mortar never reach the masons; whatever Bellmire is building stops where it stands.
No lime comes in. The mortar runs out and the walls stop at the course they are on.
The masons have stone and nothing to set it with. Building halts.
Mortar fails first, then the build. Nothing rises while Tibb holds the kiln.
No mortar reaches the masons, and every half-built wall in Bellmire stays half-built.
Lime and mortar are taken on the road; building stops where it stands.
No lime reaches the masons; whatever Bellmire is building waits.
cleared_alt: The kiln is cold and empty. Mad Tibb is walked back to town the colour of chalk.
Mad Tibb comes out of the kiln for the last time. The lime carts run.
The Lime Kiln is cleared. The masons set stone again.
Tibb's crew are washed, chained and done. Mortar reaches the walls.
The kiln goes cold. Mad Tibb is led off, still laughing, still white.
The kiln is emptied and Mad Tibb is brought down the road, white to the elbows.
The Lime Kiln is cleared. The mortar comes through, and so does the building.

bandit_camps.name: The Sunken Boat
bandit_camps.appears: Hask has swamped a boat across the narrows and robs whoever stops to haul it clear.
bandit_camps.while: The narrows are blocked; barges wait, and what they carry spoils in the hold.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Sunken Boat burns to the waterline. Hask swims for the far bank and is met on it.
appears_alt: Hask has swamped a boat across the narrows and robs whoever stops to haul it clear.
There is a hull across the narrows that did not sink by accident. Hask put it there.
The narrows are blocked and the bank is watched. Hask is working the river.
A barge crew went to clear a wreck and came back with nothing. Hask's wreck.
Another hull lies across the narrows, and Hask the Ferryman's Brother stands on the bank with a boathook.
A boat is down in the narrows, and Hask is waiting for someone to stop for it.
Hask has sunk a boat in the narrows again.
while_alt: The narrows are blocked; barges wait, and what they carry spoils in the hold.
Nothing passes the narrows. The barges sit and the cargo turns.
The river queues at the wreck - goods rot in the hold while they wait.
Barges stack up at the narrows and their loads go bad where they lie.
Barges queue at the blocked narrows, and their cargo spoils while they wait.
The narrows are blocked; barges wait and their cargo spoils.
Barges queue at the narrows; whatever they carry goes bad in the hold.
cleared_alt: The Sunken Boat burns to the waterline. Hask swims for the far bank and is met on it.
The narrows are cleared of hull and of Hask. The barges move.
The wreck is dragged out. The river runs and the holds keep their cargo.
Hask takes to the water and does not come out of it. The narrows are open.
The narrows are cleared and the wreck is chopped for kindling. Hask is caught on the bank.
The sunken boat is cleared and Hask is taken on the bank.
The narrows open. Hask is on the far bank, and so is the Watch.

bandit_camps.name: Blackbrier Hide
bandit_camps.appears: Iver Cutgrass has cut a camp into the blackbrier where no horse can follow.
bandit_camps.while: Foot traffic on the south track is robbed; the smaller traders stop coming at all.
bandit_camps.cleared: Blackbrier Hide is burned out. The south track carries packs again.
appears_alt: Iver Cutgrass has cut a camp into the blackbrier where no horse can follow.
There are paths cut in the blackbrier that no shepherd made. Iver Cutgrass.
A packman came in with a cut strap and no pack. Iver holds the blackbrier.
Blackbrier Hide is occupied again, and the thorns are on Iver's side.
Iver Cutgrass has grown a camp into the blackbrier. Nobody saw it planted.
Iver Cutgrass is in the brier again, where no horse can reach him.
The south track has been quiet since Iver Cutgrass moved back in.
while_alt: Foot traffic on the south track is robbed; the smaller traders stop coming at all.
Packmen are stripped on the south track. The small trade dries up.
The south track is walked only by Iver's crew - the little traders stay home.
Every pack on the south track is Iver's. The small sellers stop arriving.
Walkers on the south track are robbed, and the small traders quit the track.
The south track is robbed on foot; the small traders stop coming.
Pedlars on the south track are stripped, and the smaller trade dies off.
cleared_alt: Blackbrier Hide is burned out. The south track carries packs again.
Iver Cutgrass is pulled out of the thorns. The packmen come back.
The blackbrier is cut to the root. The south track is safe on foot.
Iver's paths are burned shut. The small traders fill the market again.
The brier is cut back to the root. Iver Cutgrass is found in the middle, scratched to ribbons.
The brier is burned back to bare ground. Iver Cutgrass has nowhere left to hide.
Blackbrier Hide is cleared. The pedlars use the south track again.

bandit_camps.name: The Charcoal Camp
bandit_camps.appears: Mother Soot and her burners hold the charcoal stands above the wood.
bandit_camps.while: Charcoal runs short; the forge works half days and smith prices climb.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Charcoal Camp is taken. The forge burns a full day again.
appears_alt: Mother Soot and her burners hold the charcoal stands above the wood.
The charcoal stands are smoking for somebody else. Mother Soot is up there.
No charcoal came down the wood road. Mother Soot holds the stands.
Mother Soot is back in the burns, and the smoke is hers now.
Mother Soot has put her burners in the charcoal stands, and the smoke goes up black and unsold.
Mother Soot is above the wood with her burners, and the stands are hers.
Smoke is rising from the charcoal stands, and it is the wrong smoke. Mother Soot has them.
while_alt: Charcoal runs short; the forge works half days and smith prices climb.
The forge banks its fire by noon - half a day's work, and the smith's price up.
No charcoal, no heat. The forge shuts early and charges more for what it finishes.
Charcoal comes in by the sack instead of the cart. Half days at the forge, dearer iron.
The charcoal stops, the forge keeps half days, and every smith charges more.
Charcoal stops coming down; the forge works half days and smith prices climb.
The forge cannot get charcoal; it works half days and prices rise.
cleared_alt: The Charcoal Camp is taken. The forge burns a full day again.
Mother Soot is put out. The charcoal carts come down the wood road.
The stands are the town's again - full days at the forge and an honest price.
Mother Soot's burners scatter. The forge keeps its fire till dark.
The stands are taken. Mother Soot is led out, sooty to the elbows.
The Charcoal Camp is taken, and Mother Soot's burners are sent down black.
The stands burn for the forge again. Mother Soot does not.

bandit_camps.name: The Rook Field
bandit_camps.appears: Carrow Dace has set his crew in the rook field, where the crop stands tall enough to hide a man.
bandit_camps.while: Harvest carts are stopped at the field edge; grain comes in short at the measure.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Rook Field is cut early and cleared. The measure fills honestly again.
appears_alt: Carrow Dace has set his crew in the rook field, where the crop stands tall enough to hide a man.
The rook field is full of more than crop. Carrow Dace is in it.
A harvest cart was stopped at the field edge by men who came out of the wheat. Carrow Dace.
There are paths trodden through the rook field that lead nowhere good. Carrow Dace holds it.
The rooks have left the field, and Carrow Dace's crew have taken their place.
Carrow Dace is in the rook field, and the crop is tall enough to hide a crew.
The rooks went up all at once. Carrow Dace is in the field.
while_alt: Harvest carts are stopped at the field edge; grain comes in short at the measure.
The carts are bled at the field edge. The measure never fills.
Grain goes into the rook field and not out of it. The measure reads short.
Carrow takes his share off the cart. The granary counts the difference.
Carts are turned back at the field edge, and the grain comes up short at the measure.
Harvest carts are stopped at the field edge; the measure comes up short.
Grain is taken at the field and the measure runs short.
cleared_alt: The Rook Field is cut early and cleared. The measure fills honestly again.
Carrow Dace is flushed out of the wheat. The harvest comes in whole.
The rook field is stubble and no shelter. The measure reads true.
Carrow's crew are cut down with the crop. Grain arrives full weight.
The Rook Field is cut open. Carrow Dace is found sitting very still in the stubble.
The Rook Field is cut down, and Carrow Dace with it.
The field is cut early. The measure fills, and honestly.

bandit_camps.name: The Salt Road Camp
bandit_camps.appears: Tam Pell has taken the salt road where it narrows, and charges the narrow part.
bandit_camps.while: Salt and cured stores arrive dear; preserved food in town spoils faster for want of it.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Salt Road Camp is broken. Salt comes in at the old price.
appears_alt: Tam Pell has taken the salt road where it narrows, and charges the narrow part.
The salt road has a price on it now. Tam Pell set it.
Salt came in at twice the money. Tam Pell holds the narrows.
Tam Pell is camped where the salt road pinches, and nothing passes cheap.
Tam Pell has staked out the narrow part of the salt road and is tallying every cart.
Tam Pell is at the narrow part of the salt road again, with his hand out.
Salt has gone up in the market. Tam Pell is on the salt road.
while_alt: Salt and cured stores arrive dear; preserved food in town spoils faster for want of it.
Salt costs double. What the town cures does not keep.
Dear salt, thin curing - the stores turn before they are eaten.
Tam's price is on every barrel of salt. The preserved food goes off early.
Salt arrives dear and late, so cured food in town goes off sooner.
Salt and cured stores come in dear; preserved food spoils faster for want of salt.
The salt trade pays Tam at the narrows, and what reaches town is short and dear.
cleared_alt: The Salt Road Camp is broken. Salt comes in at the old price.
Tam Pell is taken off the narrows. The curing sheds are busy again.
The salt road is free. The stores keep their weight and their season.
Tam Pell charges nobody now. Salt is salt-priced.
Tam Pell's tally ends. The salt road is open, and salt is cheap again.
The Salt Road Camp is broken. Tam Pell pays his own toll, in the Watch house.
The salt road is open. The price falls back.

bandit_camps.name: The Beekeeper's Hut
bandit_camps.appears: Hollis Grin has turned the beekeeper out of his own hut and kept the bees.
bandit_camps.while: Honey, wax and candle stock dry up; the apothecary brews slower without wax.
bandit_camps.cleared: Hollis Grin is stung out of the hut. The beekeeper goes back to his bees.
appears_alt: Hollis Grin has turned the beekeeper out of his own hut and kept the bees.
The beekeeper is in town with nothing but stings. Hollis Grin has his hut.
Hollis Grin is in the hives, and he is not asking the bees.
No wax, no honey, and a grinning man up at the hut. Hollis Grin.
Hollis Grin is in the beekeeper's hut. The beekeeper is in the ditch outside it.
Hollis Grin is in the beekeeper's hut. The beekeeper is in the ditch.
The bees are humming over a different man's roof. Hollis Grin has the hut.
while_alt: Honey, wax and candle stock dry up; the apothecary brews slower without wax.
No wax in town - candles run out and the apothecary's work slows.
Honey and wax both stop. Candles get scarce and the brews take longer.
The hives feed Hollis. Candle stock empties and the apothecary waits on wax.
No honey, no wax, no candles; the apothecary brews at half speed for want of wax.
Honey, wax and candles dry up; the apothecary brews slower without wax.
No wax reaches town; the apothecary slows and the candle stalls empty.
cleared_alt: Hollis Grin is stung out of the hut. The beekeeper goes back to his bees.
The hut is handed back. Wax, honey and candles come down again.

Hollis Grin is stung out of the hut and the beekeeper goes home to his bees.
The hut is the beekeeper's again, and the wax comes to market.

bandit_camps.name: The Dry Ferry
bandit_camps.appears: Nils Odd has taken the old ferry landing upriver and runs his own crossing at his own rates.

bandit_camps.cleared: The Dry Ferry is sunk at its moorings. The river comes back to the Ford.

while_alt: Half the river trade goes around Bellmire entirely; the Ford takes less each day.

Nils takes the crossings Bellmire used to. The Ford's take falls daily.

cleared_alt: The Dry Ferry is sunk at its moorings. The river comes back to the Ford.

The Dry Ferry is sunk and Nils Odd with it. The river comes back to the Ford.

bandit_camps.name: The Ox Road Camp
bandit_camps.appears: Bram Sallow holds the ox road and takes a beast from every team that passes.
bandit_camps.while: Hauling costs double; stone, timber and grain all arrive late and dear.
bandit_camps.cleared: The Ox Road Camp is cleared out. The teams come in whole.
appears_alt: Bram Sallow holds the ox road and takes a beast from every team that passes.

Bram Sallow is on the ox road again, counting teams.
A team came in a beast short. Bram Sallow has the ox road.
while_alt: Hauling costs double; stone, timber and grain all arrive late and dear.
Every load costs twice to move. Stone, timber and grain all come in late.
Teams come in a beast short, so everything hauled is slower and dearer.

Every haul costs twice as much, and stone, timber and grain come in dear and late.
Every team pays a beast at the camp; hauling costs double and stone, timber and grain come late and dear.

cleared_alt: The Ox Road Camp is cleared out. The teams come in whole.
Bram Sallow's herd is given back. Hauling costs what it should.
The ox road is safe for a team again. Stone, timber and grain arrive on time.

There is a crack in the quarry floor with something coming out of it in file.
Cave centipedes are climbing up through the Split Stone, and none of them is small.
The Split Stone is split a little wider every night, and something long keeps coming out of it.
Something long is coming up through the Split Stone again.
The quarry crew came home early. The Split Stone is open.
while_alt: The quarry stands idle; building work in town stops where the stone runs out.
No quarrying while they come up. Building stops when the last stone is laid.
The quarry is abandoned - the builds run until the stone does, and then stop.
Nothing is cut at the quarry. Every build halts at the end of the stock.
The quarry sits idle, and building in town stops when the stone runs out.
The quarry stands idle; building in town stops where the stone runs out.
No stone is cut; the builders use up what they have and stop.
cleared_alt: The Split Stone is sealed and the nest burned. The quarry rings again.
The crack is filled and fired. The quarry is cut again.
The Split Stone is cleared. The stone comes up and the builds go on.
The nest is burned to the floor. The quarry works.
The crack is sealed with burning pitch. The quarry rings again.
The Split Stone is sealed. The quarry rings.
The centipedes are burned out and the quarry opens.

monster_camps.name: The Hog Mire
monster_camps.appears: The mire boars have grown wrong and bold, and they hold the lower fields.
monster_camps.while: The lower fields are rooted up; this season's crop is halved where they walk.
monster_camps.cleared: The Hog Mire is cleared, and the town eats well for a week.
appears_alt: The mire boars have grown wrong and bold again, and they hold the lower fields.
The lower fields are turned over and nobody ploughed them. Mire boars.
There are boars in the lower fields the size of ponies, and they are not leaving.
The Hog Mire is up in the lower fields, and they have no fear left.
The boars in the mire have stopped running from people. They have started running at them.
The mire boars are in the lower fields again.
The ground is torn up in the low fields.
while_alt: The lower fields are rooted up; this season's crop is halved where they walk.
Where they root, the crop is lost - half the lower harvest goes with them.
The lower fields are ploughed by snout. Half that crop will not come in.
They root the lower fields nightly; the season's yield there is cut in half.
The lower fields are rooted up; this season's crop is halved wherever they roam.
The lower fields are torn up; the season's crop is halved wherever they walk.
Boars root the lower fields and the crop is half what it should be.
cleared_alt: The Hog Mire is cleared, and the town eats well for a week.
The boars are put down in the lower fields. What is left of the crop stands.
The Hog Mire is finished. There is pork at every table and crop in the rest.
The lower fields are the town's again, and dinner is settled.
The mire is cleared of tusks. Bellmire feasts and mends fences.
The Hog Mire is cleared, and the town eats pork.
The boars are driven off. The fields are sound again.

monster_camps.name: The Chalk Pit
monster_camps.appears: The chalk pit has filled with crawling things made mostly of other things' bones.
monster_camps.while: Lime and chalk stop coming up; mortar runs out and the masons down tools.
monster_camps.cleared: The Chalk Pit is cleared to the floor. The masons take up tools again.
appears_alt: The chalk pit has filled again with crawling things made mostly of other things' bones.
Something is assembling itself in the chalk pit out of what it finds there.
The chalk pit is crawling, and the crawlers are not whole creatures.
Bone crawlers have taken the chalk pit, and they are built out of the pit's leavings.
The chalk pit is rattling. It is full of things that should not be able to climb.
Something white is crawling in the chalk pit.
The chalk pit is moving again.
while_alt: Lime and chalk stop coming up; mortar runs out and the masons down tools.
No chalk, no lime, no mortar. The masons stop where they stand.
The pit yields nothing. The mortar runs out and the trowels go down.
Chalk and lime both stop. The masons have nothing to set with.
No chalk or lime comes up, the mortar runs out, and the masons put down their tools.
Lime and chalk stop coming up; the mortar runs out and the masons down tools.
No chalk reaches the masons; the mortar runs out and work stops.
cleared_alt: The Chalk Pit is cleared to the floor. The masons take up tools again.
The crawlers are broken up and burned. The chalk comes up.
The Chalk Pit is emptied. Lime runs and the mortar is mixed.
The pit is clean to the bottom. The masons work.
The pit is cleared and the bones are carted off. The masons can work again.
The Chalk Pit is cleared to the floor.
The crawlers are put down and the pit gives chalk again.

wandering_boss.name: The Scarred Lord
wandering_boss.appears: A lord has climbed out of the scar and walks the open country - and it has grown to match the town it hunts.
wandering_boss.while: It razes an outlying farm each day it roams, and draws the dark along behind it.
wandering_boss.cleared: The wandering lord falls in the open field. Bellmire drags the body home as proof.
wandering_boss.note: Scales to the town's level: a lesser lord early, a greater lord once Bellmire is a city. Reuse the eight canon lords; never a new one.
appears_alt: Something that should be under the scar is walking the open country, and it has grown to fit the town it is coming for.
A lord has climbed out of the dark and taken to the fields. It gets larger the nearer it comes.
The scar let one out. It is wearing the shape of the town's own strength.
A lord is out of the scar and loose in the open, and it is bigger than the last one that tried.
The deep sent one up into daylight. It has the measure of the town already.
A crowned thing walks the fields, and the holdings empty ahead of it.
A lord is out of the scar and walking under the sky, and it has grown into the town's own measure.
Something crowned has left the dark and taken the open road.
The scar gave one up. It is in the fields, and it is the size of Bellmire's best year.
A lord walks the open country, and the holdings go dark ahead of it.
One of them is out. It came up into daylight and did not mind the daylight.
A lord is loose above ground, grown to match whatever Bellmire has become.
The deep sent a crowned thing up the stair and out the door.
A lord is in the open fields, and it is wearing the town's own strength for size.
A lord is walking the open country, and the fields remember its shadow before it passes.
The scar's own captain has taken to the road. It grows as the town grows, and so does the fear.
Something with a name is crossing the open fields, scaled to the size of the town that must meet it.
A lord out of the dark crosses the farmland at its own slow pace, and the dogs have gone silent.
The wandering lord has been seen at the treeline, exactly as large as it needs to be to frighten you.
A canon lord has left the scar and is walking up the valley. Bellmire is on the way, and knows it.
The scar has sent one of its lords up to walk the country. It looks about the size of Bellmire's next worst day.
A tall dark shape crosses the far hills at dusk, and the shepherds come in early.
The lord that climbed out of the scar has grown to fit the town it hunts, and it is taking its time.
A lord walks the open fields in daylight and does not hurry. The farm dogs go quiet.
Something from below stands on the ridge and counts Bellmire's roofs.
The scar's lord is above ground, and has the look of a thing that was promised a town.
The Scarred Lord is walking the open country again, bigger than the last time.
A farmhand ran in from the fields to say a lord is out and walking.
The scar has let a lord out, and it has grown to the size of the town it hunts.
while_alt: A holding goes dark each night it roams, and the dark follows it home.
It burns an outlying farm a day and drags the deep country along behind it.
Nothing stays settled where it walks; the far farms empty ahead of it.
A farm goes to ash each day it walks, and the dark thickens where it slept.
The outlying holdings fall one by one, and what follows it does not leave.
It takes a holding a day and leaves the deep sitting on the ruin.
It burns one outlying holding a day, and the dark it drags stays on the ruin.
A farm a day goes to ash, and the deep settles where the farm was.
The far holdings empty ahead of it; each one lost costs the town its yield.
It takes a holding each day it roams, and the ground behind it does not recover.
One outlying farm razed a day, and monsters thicken in its wake.
Each day it walks costs Bellmire a holding and leaves the dark sitting on it.
A holding a day, burned, and what follows the lord does not leave when it does.
The outlying farms fall one a day, and the deep moves up into the gaps.
Each day it walks, another farm goes dark, and the dark does not go back.
An outlying farm falls every day it roams, and the night comes earlier behind it.
The fields it crosses lie fallow after. The people on them do not come back.
It keeps the pace of a funeral and razes a holding a day.
Another farm lost with every dawn. The dark trails it like a train.
It razes one steading a day, and the stillness after is the worst of it.
Each day it walks, an outlying holding is razed, and the dark it drags settles on the ruin.
One farm a day goes down to ash, and the dark stays on the ground where it stood.
It razes a holding at every dawn, and the shadows it leaves do not lift.
The outlying farms fall one by one, a day apiece, each ruin left darker than the last.
Every day it roams, one more steading is burned flat and haunted for it.
A farm a day is razed, and the dark follows the lord home and lingers on the wreck.
It razes one outlying farm for every day it roams, and leaves the dark on the ruin.
Each day it walks, another outlying holding is razed and the dark stays on the ground.
One farm a day goes down while it roams, and the dark stays where it stood.
cleared_alt: The wandering lord goes down in the open field, in daylight, in front of everyone.
It falls at last on honest ground. Bellmire hauls the carcass back as proof.
The lord is put down outside the walls. The farms come back one cart at a time.
The lord falls in the open, under the sky, and the field keeps the mark.
It goes down outside the walls. The farms are back inside a week.
The wandering lord is killed in daylight. Bellmire makes a cartload of proof.
The lord goes down in the open field, in daylight, with the whole town watching.
It falls outside the walls. The farms are reoccupied within the week.
The wandering lord is put down on honest ground and dragged home as proof.
It dies in the open. The field keeps the mark and the town keeps the story.
The lord falls under the sky. The holdings light their fires again that night.
Put down in the stubble, in front of everyone. The dark goes back down.
The crowned thing falls in the open country, and the far farms come back.
It is killed in daylight, outside the walls, and Bellmire makes a cartload of proof.
The wandering lord falls in the open, the field goes red, and then it is only a field.
It drops at last in the sunlight, and Bellmire hauls the proof back by cart.
Its walk ends in the long grass. The town carries the head home, or nobody would believe it.
The wandering lord is brought down in the open country, and the dark it dragged behind it thins and goes.
The field holds the body and the farms hold their breath. Then both let go.
It is done in daylight, which the scar did not expect. The town counts the cost, then the cart.
The lord falls on open ground, and Bellmire drags the proof home on a hurdle.
The wandering lord is dead in the barley. The dark lifts off the ruins, slowly.
It goes down at last, and Bellmire counts the farms it will have to rebuild.
The lord's long walk ends in a ditch. The town cheers, then goes to look at the damage.
The lord is brought down in the open. The delvers bring the head; the farmers bring the bill.
The country is its own again. The lord lies where it fell, and the crows are already deciding.
The wandering lord is down in the open field, and Bellmire hauls the body home.
The Scarred Lord falls in the open country. The carts go out to fetch it.
The lord is dead in the field, and the dark lifts off the ruins.

events._note_variants_c24: Widened C-cycle 24: wandering_boss appears_alt / while_alt / cleared_alt 6 -> 14 each. There is still only one wandering boss, so these three are the lines that repeat most. Every while_alt states the same implementable cost as the canonical while - one outlying holding razed per day it roams, and the dark it drags persists on the ruin. name, appears, while, cleared and note are UNCHANGED. Additive; dead until wired.
events._note_variants_c29: Widened C-cycle 29: every bandit camp (20) and every monster camp (19) now carries appears_alt / while_alt / cleared_alt - 4 lines each, the same key shape wandering_boss already uses. Each camp previously had exactly ONE appears, while and cleared line, so the second time the same camp spawned on a stream it read word for word. Each while_alt states the SAME implementable cost as that camp's canonical `while` - reworded, never widened: no alt adds an effect the canonical line does not already state, so the desktop worker can implement the cost once per camp and pick any line to show. name, leader, of, appears, while and cleared are UNCHANGED on every camp. No new camp, no new named leader. Additive; dead until wired.
events._note_variants_c47: Widened C-cycle 47: wandering_boss appears_alt / while_alt / cleared_alt 20 -> 26 each, and every bandit camp (20) and monster camp (19) gains one more appears_alt, while_alt and cleared_alt (4 -> 5). Every new while_alt restates the SAME implementable cost as that camp's canonical while - reworded, never widened; the wandering boss's still razes one outlying holding per day and leaves the dark on the ruin. name, leader, of, appears, while, cleared and note are UNCHANGED. Additive; dead until wired.
events._note_variants_c64: C-64: +2 appears_alt, +2 while_alt, +2 cleared_alt on every bandit camp (20) and monster camp (19), and +3 each on wandering_boss (243 lines). Every new while_alt restates the SAME implementable cost as that camp's canonical while - reworded, never widened. name, leader, of, appears, while, cleared and note UNCHANGED. Additive; dead until wired.

growth_tiers._note: Town growth stages (D31/D32) - the town levels far too fast, so this is a long, earned climb. For each: the stage name, the crier's line on reaching it, and what a viewer should SEE appear. Complements town_levels_for_the_desktop (coarser, 7 levels). Dead until wired.

tiers.name: Crossing
tiers.crier: A handful of huts at a river crossing. Somebody calls it Bellmire.
tiers.see: Three or four huts, a cart, a cookfire.

tiers.name: Hamlet
tiers.crier: Bellmire is a hamlet now - a well dug, and a reason to stay.
tiers.see: A well, a few more homes, a fenced garden or two.

tiers.name: The Guild Post
tiers.crier: The guild plants a post at Bellmire. The post has a door, and the door is kept.
tiers.see: The guild post building, and the town's first lamp.

tiers.name: Village
tiers.crier: Bellmire is a village. The scar has a name, and so do we.
tiers.see: Homes clustered along a cart-track, chickens, a shared pen.

tiers.name: Market Day
tiers.crier: Market day comes to Bellmire. Measure the grain.
tiers.see: A market square with a few stalls, and the first outside traders.

tiers.name: The Chapel
tiers.crier: A chapel and a bell-tower rise. The bell has no clapper, and rings anyway.
tiers.see: The temple and its tower, and a small graveyard behind it.

tiers.name: Craft Row
tiers.crier: The smiths and masons raise Craft Row. Count the flasks.
tiers.see: Workshops trailing smoke, a forge-glow, the mill wheel turning.

tiers.name: The Garrison
tiers.crier: Bellmire raises a garrison. The guard has a yard now - and a Commander.
tiers.see: Barracks and a training yard, guards on patrol, E3PO up on the wall.

tiers.name: Market Town
tiers.crier: Bellmire stands as a proper market town. The caravans know the road.
tiers.see: A paved square, more districts, a busy Ford with its Ferryman.

tiers.name: The First Wall
tiers.crier: Stone goes up where the fields used to stop. Keep the door.
tiers.see: A low wall around the town's heart, and a gatehouse over the road.

tiers.name: Walled Town
tiers.crier: Bellmire is a walled town now. Let them come.
tiers.see: A full curtain wall, corner towers, a district banner on each quarter.

tiers.name: City in all but Charter
tiers.crier: Bellmire is a city in all but the charter - and the scar is deeper than it has ever been.
tiers.see: Dense districts, a second ring of homes outside the wall, traffic at every gate.

townsfolk._note: C-48 / WORK_PLAN C5 - the townsfolk as a community (words half of D36). Dead until wired; content worker never touches code. Additive. KEY SHAPE: names{given_f,given_m,family,by_names} -> a townsperson = one given name (given_f or given_m by body) + EITHER one family OR one by_name (never both); trades{<trade_key>:{label,from_tier,bark[],morning[],midday[],evening[],night[]}} -> bind a trade whose from_tier <= current growth tier (1-12, see growth_tiers.tiers); speak bark[] as an ambient shout, and morning/midday/evening/night[] as the activity line for that part of the day; react{raid,disaster,festival,caravan,growth,hunger,hero_falls,hero_rich}[] -> a generic spoken line for any townsperson when the game raises that event; remember[] -> entries {when,n,[kind],lines[]} held back until the condition token is true (see _conditions); cast[] -> 10 fully written named townsfolk (id,name,trade,from_tier,bio, bark[] EXTRA to the trade's own bark[] so the cast speaks both, morning/midday/evening/night one activity line each, react{8 events: one line each}, remember[2] same shape as the top-level remember) to bind as notables if the game wants authored characters. No line states a dungeon floor count.

_conditions.disaster_repeat_season: the same disaster kind (entry.kind) has struck n times this season
_conditions.disaster_streak: n disasters of any kind in a row without a calm spell between
_conditions.raid_survived_total: the town has survived n raids in total
_conditions.raid_streak: n raids in a row without a quiet spell
_conditions.long_peace_days: n in-game days since the last raid
_conditions.hunger_after_growth: hunger event raised within one growth tier-up of the last stage change
_conditions.festival_after_disaster: a festival is raised within one day of a disaster ending
_conditions.festival_after_raid: a festival is raised within one day of a raid ending
_conditions.hero_fell_repeat: n heroes have fallen within the same in-game day
_conditions.hero_fell_then_returned: a fallen viewer hero has returned to roster
_conditions.caravan_missed: a scheduled caravan did not arrive
_conditions.caravan_arrived_after_hunger: a caravan arrives while the hunger event is active or just ended
_conditions.tier_reached_recent: the town reached a new growth tier within the last in-game day
_conditions.e3po_withdrew_recent: E3PO withdrew to barracks within the last in-game day
_conditions.e3po_returned_recent: E3PO returned from barracks within the last in-game day

ferryman.label: Ferryman
bark: Mind the rope, it bites.
One copper across, two if you argue.
The Ford was here first. We just pay it.
River's up. Hold your hat and your tongue.
Never ferried a ghost. Ferried a few who looked it.
Careful - the scar's still warm under the water.
morning: Checks the ferry rope for fray before the first crossing.
Bails last night's rain out of the flat boat.
Wipes the rope-burn from his palms and thumbs the knot.
midday: Poles a cartload of turnips over, muttering the whole way.
Eats cold barley by the landing, one eye on the far bank.
Tells a passenger the ford is shallow. It is not.
evening: Ties the ferry up and counts the day's coppers twice.
Sits on the jetty, feet dangling, naming the fish he missed.
Hauls the flat boat up on the mud and checks the plank.
night: Sleeps in the boat so the river never forgets him.
Hangs a lantern at the landing for anyone still out on the road.
Rows nobody anywhere, to keep the oars from forgetting.

fishwife.label: Fishwife
bark: Trout! Fresh as a slap and twice as honest!
Three coppers the carp, and the carp has opinions.
Buy a pike, hear a lie. Buy two, hear the truth.
Eels, love - they wriggle, so you know they're fresh.
The river gives, the river takes. I only sell what it gives.
Scales on my hands, silver in my purse. Fair trade.
morning: Guts the morning catch on the landing stones, gulls circling.
Chalks the day's prices on a slate and underlines the carp twice.
Lays out the catch in rows, biggest at the front.
midday: Hawks trout across the market, voice like a rusty hinge.
Argues a copper off a cheese-monger, and wins.
Sells a perch and swears it is a pike.
evening: Packs the unsold eels in wet reeds and curses the heat.
Scrubs her knife in the river and hums off-key.
Rinses the slate and rubs out the day's prices.
night: Smokes the last fish over a low fire, grumbling.
Counts silver by lamplight and does not share the total.
Wraps a heel of fish in dock leaf for the cat at the door.

reed_cutter.label: Reed-Cutter
bark: Reed's thick this year. Thatch will be cheap.
Don't walk the soft ground. The marsh keeps what it takes.
Cut at the root, not the tip. Everything worth knowing, that.
Frogs are loud tonight. Means rain, or means frogs.
The marsh hums if you stand quiet. I don't stand quiet.
Bundles for sale. Bring your own string.
morning: Wades out at first light with a hooked knife and a bad back.
Stacks yesterday's reeds to dry against the north wall.
Tests the knife on a thumbnail and nods.
midday: Binds reed bundles with a speed that shames the guild clerks.
Rests on a stump, chewing a stalk, watching the water.
Carries a bundle taller than himself and does not complain.
evening: Hauls the last bundles in as the midges rise.
Smears mud on his neck against the bites and swears at the sky.
Counts the day's bundles out loud, twice, same number.
night: Listens to the marsh from his doorstep, one boot off.
Mends his cutting knife by the fire, murmuring to it.
Hangs his wet boots by the door and sits on the step.

farmer.label: Farmer
bark: Measure the grain. Count the flasks. Keep the door. Plough the field.
Rain's late. Mutter to the sky, it helps nobody.
Good soil by the Ford. Bad luck by the scar.
My hands remember what the crop forgets.
Turnips again. Be glad it isn't thistles.
If it grows, it feeds Bellmire. If it doesn't, we argue.
morning: Drives the ox out before the dew has dried.
Walks the furrows, kicking clods, finding fault.
Looks at the sky, then the ox, then the sky again.
midday: Hoes the bean rows with a rhythm like a slow drum.
Eats bread and onion in the shade of a cart, sweating.
Mends a hurdle with a knotted cord and a short oath.
evening: Hauls a sack to the granary and counts it into the ledger.
Leans on the fence rail, appraising a neighbour's wheat.
Washes the dirt from his arms at the trough.
night: Checks the ox, checks the gate, checks the sky, checks again.
Sits up with the lamp low, tallying the harvest and the debt.
Falls asleep at the table with the spoon still in his hand.

well_keeper.label: Well-Keeper
bark: Water's sweet this morning. Don't ask me why. I never do.
Queue's moving. It was a queue yesterday, too.
Wind the rope slow. The bucket remembers.
Second well dug and the first still gets the glory.
Sweeter than ale and half the price. Drink.
Never drop a coin down it. The bottom is listening.
morning: Draws the first bucket and tastes it, solemn as a priest.
Sweeps the well-yard and shoos a goose off the stone lip.
Checks the rope for rot before anyone asks for water.
midday: Winds bucket after bucket for a line of grumbling housewives.
Mends a frayed rope with a tongue-clucking patience.
Pours a dipper for a tired carter and takes no coin.
evening: Rinses the lip stone and sets the lid against the evening dust.
Listens down the shaft for the old echo, then nods.
Wipes the bucket rim dry and hangs it up.
night: Latches the well-gate, jingling the key like a small bell.
Sits near the shaft in the dark, claiming it hums.
Counts the buckets drawn and chalks it on the post.

herder.label: Herder
bark: Easy, easy - they only look stupid.
Sheep go where the grass is. Folk go where the grain is.
Hup, you woolly fools! Mind the road!
Wolves in the hills? Not on my watch. Possibly on someone's.
Fleece is good this season. Ask about the price after.
A good dog is worth three hands. Two dogs, a miracle.
morning: Counts the flock out through the gate, lips moving.
Checks a ewe's hoof and talks to her as if she'd understand.
Walks the fence line and finds where the gap was.
midday: Lounges on a hillock with a crook, eyes half-shut, ears fully open.
Shears a sheep with the unconcern of long practice.
Whittles a peg with the flock grazing at his feet.
evening: Brings the flock home dusty and complaining, himself included.
Sits with the dog, sharing a heel of bread.
Wipes the dog's paws and checks for thorns.
night: Folds the sheep and counts them again, then once more for luck.
Whistles low through the dark so the flock knows he's there.
Leans on the pen rail and says goodnight to each ewe.

baker.label: Baker
bark: Hot loaves! Hot loaves! The bell may have no clapper but my oven rings true!
Oat cake, rye cake, no cake - choose.
Bread for the Ford, bread for the road, bread for the dead.
Buy early. The guard buys the rest.
Burnt crust is free. Burnt pride costs extra.
Keep the door, keep the oven, keep the peace.
morning: Fires the oven before dawn and swears at the flour sack.
Kneads dough on a table scarred by forty winters.
Dusts the board with flour and scores the first loaves.
midday: Slides loaves out on a long peel, face red as the coals.
Sells the heel to a child with a wink and nothing else.
Sets a tray of buns to cool and watches them like a hawk.
evening: Sweeps the oven floor and counts the unsold, grimly.
Slices a stale loaf for the beggar at the back door.
Wraps the last loaf in cloth for the morning.
night: Banks the coals low and sets the dough to rise for dawn.
Falls asleep on a flour sack, snoring like a bellows.
Rakes the ash from the oven mouth and shuts the iron door.

guild_clerk.label: Guild Clerk
bark: Papers, please. And a coin, and your name, and the right door.
The guild keeps accounts. The guild always keeps accounts.
Heroes come, heroes go. The ledger stays.
Sign here. And here. Not there - that's the other contract.
Quills cost more than swords, this year.
The post has a door and the door is kept. By me.
morning: Opens the guild post, unlocks the ledger and polishes a bronze seal.
Sharpens three quills and curses the ink.
Blots yesterday's page and files it under the right hero.
midday: Stamps a hero's contract with a thunk of finality.
Argues a clause with a merchant, tapping the ledger like scripture.
Reads out a contract slowly so no one can say they missed a line.
evening: Totals the day's accounts and hums when the sum is good.
Locks the strongbox with a key on a string around his neck.
Ties the day's papers in a bundle and sets them in the strongbox.
night: Reads one more contract by candlelight, not trusting the first reading.
Locks the post door, checks it, then checks it again.
Trims the candle, signs one last page, and does not hurry.

carter.label: Carter
bark: Mind your toes! This ox has no brakes and one opinion!
Grain in, goods out, pay me what's owed.
Roads are rough. The Ford is rougher. Hold on.
Axle's fine. It always sounds like that.
I've hauled for the guild, the Chief, and once a dead man. He paid best.
Heave, ox. Heave, or be stew.
morning: Greases the axle, whistling through the grease.
Harnesses the ox and speaks to it of delicate matters.
Checks the ox's yoke for rubs before he loads a thing.
midday: Hauls a heaped cart through the market, shouting at everyone.
Unloads sacks at the granary, shoulder first.
Wedges a stone under a wheel and eats his bread on the tailboard.
evening: Unhitches the ox and rubs down its flanks.
Counts the day's loads into a battered tally book.
Sweeps the cart bed and stacks the empty sacks.
night: Sleeps under his cart with the ox for company.
Checks wheel spokes by lamplight, murmuring prayers to the road.
Pulls a tarp over the load and ties it three times.

smith.label: Smith
bark: Iron wants hitting. So do some customers.
Hot work! Stand back or smell like bacon.
A blade is only as honest as the hand that quenched it.
Nails, hinges, hooks - the town runs on small iron.
Bring me ore and patience. I'll supply the noise.
The scar eats spells, not steel. Steel I can fix.
morning: Rakes the forge awake and feeds it charcoal.
Sorts yesterday's bent nails for the scrap pile.
Lays out his tongs in order and tests the bellows.
midday: Hammers a glowing bar, sparks flying, ears long since ruined.
Dunks a blade in the trough with a hiss like a snake.
Hammers a hinge flat and holds it to the light.
evening: Banks the forge and wipes soot into a worse arrangement.
Counts the day's horseshoes into a clanking sack.
Sweeps the scale from the anvil into a bucket.
night: Sleeps by the cooling anvil, ringing faintly in his ears.
Hangs the tongs on their hook, one by one, like a ritual.
Quenches the last bar and lets the dark take the forge.

brewer.label: Brewer
bark: Ale! Thick enough to chew and strong enough to forget why!
The marsh makes the malt. The Ford makes the water. I make the mistakes.
Drink up. Tomorrow's problems are brewed by tomorrow.
Never trust a brewer who tastes his own work. Or one who doesn't.
Barley, hops, a prayer. Mostly the prayer.
Bellmire ale - bad for the liver, good for the legend.
morning: Stirs the mash with a paddle taller than a child.
Skims the froth off a vat and flicks it at the cat.
Rakes the malt over the drying floor, turning it with his feet.
midday: Rolls casks to the cart, grunting rhythm.
Tastes a ladle, frowns, adds salt, tastes again.
Sniffs the vat, nods, and tells no one what he smelled.
evening: Pours the first round at the tavern, thick fingers around the tankard.
Lets the apprentice sweep the cellar floor and watches for theft.
Chalks the day's casks on the cellar door.
night: Sleeps in the brewhouse, nose full of yeast and ambition.
Counts the barrels twice and the empties three times.
Sets a ladle on the lip of the vat and lets it sit.

miller.label: Miller
bark: Grain in, flour out, and the dust goes where it likes.
The wheel never stops. Neither do I. Neither does the bill.
A fair toll is one part in twelve. I take one in ten. Don't tell.
Flour on my hands, grievance in my heart.
Bring dry grain or bring a bucket.
Everyone eats my flour. Everyone complains about the bread.
morning: Opens the sluice and lets the wheel groan awake.
Beats the flour dust from his apron in a pale cloud.
Greases the wheel shaft and listens to it turn.
midday: Weighs a farmer's sack and weighs it again, grinning.
Sweeps the millstone, humming a threshing song.
Feels a handful of flour between thumb and finger.
evening: Closes the sluice and the wheel slows like a tired breath.
Tallies the day's toll in chalk on a beam.
Rakes the sweepings into a sack. Nothing is wasted.
night: Sleeps on a flour sack, white as a ghost, and snores.
Listens to the wheel drip in the dark, content.
Chalks the toll for the day and rubs it out with his sleeve.

chandler.label: Chandler
bark: Candles! Tallow for the poor, wax for the proud!
Lamp oil, wicks, a little hope. Light your way home.
Dark's coming. It always is. Buy light.
A candle burns once. A good one burns long.
The marsh is dark. The night is darker. My prices are fair.
Rush-lights for the thrifty. Wax for the chapel.
morning: Dips a row of wicks into hot tallow, wrinkling her nose.
Hangs finished candles on the line to harden.
Checks the tallow for impurities and skims what rises.
midday: Sells candles to a queue of tired folk.
Trims wicks with sharp little scissors and sharper remarks.
Sets a new row of candles to cool on the sill.
evening: Lights the street lamp outside her shop with ceremony.
Wipes tallow from her fingers and counts unsold stock.
Counts the day's wicks into their box.
night: Pours the last of the wax by a single, well-guarded flame.
Reads a chapbook by her own light, smug.
Snuffs the dipping pot and wipes the kettle clean.

weaver.label: Weaver
bark: Wool and flax, warp and weft. Good cloth lasts a lifetime.
The loom clacks like a tongue at a tavern.
Dye's cheap. Colour's dear. Choose.
A cloak from my hands stays dry, even in the Mire.
I weave what the town wears. I know who owes me.
Thread's strong. Debt is stronger.
morning: Warps the loom with threads in a pattern only she can read.
Shakes lint from her sleeves and starts the shuttle.
Sorts the day's thread by colour and nods at the blue.
midday: Throws the shuttle with the speed of a card sharp.
Haggles with a dyer over the price of madder.
Beats the weft tight and checks the selvage.
evening: Cuts the cloth from the loom and holds it to the window.
Folds the day's work with care and a long, tired sigh.
Hangs a finished length over the rail to show the pattern.
night: Mends a torn cloak by lamplight, humming in the half-dark.
Dreams in warp and weft, they say, and wakes with knots.
Winds the last of the wool into a ball for the morning.

innkeeper.label: Innkeeper
bark: Beds, stew, ale. The beds are straw, the stew is mostly stew.
Heroes sleep upstairs. Heroes' purses stay downstairs.
Mind the third stair. It's judged better men than you.
Room's a silver. Breakfast's a lie. Both included.
Keep your boots on and your secrets off the table.
Another tale of dungeon glory? Pay first, boast after.
morning: Changes the straw and sweeps up what the night left.
Counts the drunks asleep on the common room floor.
Airs the blankets over the rail and counts the bedbugs, fewer than last week.
midday: Ladles stew for a table of hungry delvers.
Wipes a tankard with a rag that has seen worse.
Puts a fresh barrel on the stand and tests the tap.
evening: Fills the room with noise, steam, and a bard who can't sing.
Collects coins at the bar, glaring at a friendly dispute.
Chalks the tabs on the slate by the fire.
night: Locks the cellar and the till, and sleeps with the keys under the pillow.
Hears boots on the stair and doesn't ask.
Banks the hearth, bars the door, and leaves a lamp by the stair.

chapel_keeper.label: Chapel Keeper
bark: Peace to the Ford, peace to the scar, peace to the dead.
Say a word for the fallen. They can't say it themselves.
The bell has no clapper and still it speaks, to those who listen.
Light a candle. Mind the draught. Mind the debt.
Heroes die. The chapel stays open. That is the whole sermon.
Every grave in Bellmire has a name. I check.
morning: Sweeps the chapel floor and straightens the worn pews.
Lights the morning candle for those buried the day before.
Trims the wicks and sets out the day's candles.
midday: Hears a confession in the doorway, hand on a nervous shoulder.
Reads the list of the fallen aloud, slow, unhurried.
Wipes the dust from the names cut in the stone.
evening: Closes the chapel shutters against the evening wind.
Polishes the bell's silent lip with a respectful rag.
Closes the book of the fallen and lays his hand flat on it.
night: Keeps vigil by one candle, speaking to no one.
Rings the clapperless bell with his knuckle - a hush, not a sound.
Sits in the back pew with the door left a little open.

gravedigger.label: Gravedigger
bark: Dig deep. They always come back up in the stories, never in the soil.
Spade and patience. That's the whole trade.
One more for the pile. Sorry, one more for the plot.
The scar's quiet tonight. So's my work. Pity.
I've never lost a customer. Never had a complaint.
Somebody has to. Might as well be cheerful.
morning: Marks out a fresh plot with string and a surly look.
Sharpens his spade on a stone, whistling softly.
Leans on the spade and looks at the ground a while.
midday: Digs in rhythmic silence, shirt dark with sweat.
Eats lunch on a headstone and apologises to it.
Eats his bread at the cemetery wall, in the sun.
evening: Fills in the day's work and pats the mound.
Cleans his boots at the chapel gate and nods to the dead.
Washes the clay from the spade at the pump.
night: Sits among the stones with a flask, telling them the day's news.
Counts the graves, which is a habit rather than a hobby.
Stands at the last grave with his cap in his hands.

apothecary.label: Apothecary
bark: Brews for what ails, and for what hasn't yet.
Mind the green bottle. Mind the blue. Mind everything.
Simples, salves, small mercies. Coin first.
The scar spoils the spells. It leaves the herbs alone.
A flask a day keeps the grave away. Mostly.
Hero's draught: half remedy, half marketing.
morning: Grinds herbs in a mortar the size of a head.
Labels yesterday's bottles with a spidery hand.
Opens the shutters and sets the herb bundles to air.
midday: Measures drops with a trembling, practised spoon.
Treats a hero's scraped knuckle with unwarranted gravity.
Weighs out a powder twice and writes it down.
evening: Wipes down the counter and corks the rest.
Sells one last flask to a stumbling hero, charging triple.
Wipes the scales and puts the weights back in their box.
night: Brews by candlelight, whispering rhymes to the pot.
Locks the poison shelf and hangs the key around his neck.
Reads a label three times before he lets a bottle go.

mason.label: Mason
bark: Stone doesn't argue. Clients do.
Another course on the wall. Another reason to be proud.
Mortar, line, level. The rest is patience.
The wall keeps the town. I keep the wall.
Chisel marks last longer than names.
If it leans, I've been paid too little.
morning: Mixes mortar in a trough and tests it with a thumb.
Chalks a line along the next course and squints.
Checks the plumb line and moves the stone a finger's width.
midday: Taps a block with a hammer and listens to the ring.
Lifts a stone with the sort of grunt that has a history.
Wets a block and watches how fast it drinks.
evening: Washes lime from his hands, wincing at the cracks.
Steps back to admire the day's work and finds a flaw.
Scrapes mortar from his trowel and tucks it in his belt.
night: Sleeps like a stone, which is the highest praise he knows.
Drinks to the wall, the quarry, and the knee that quit.
Runs a hand along the new course in the last light.

cooper.label: Cooper
bark: Barrels, buckets, tubs. If it holds liquid, I made it.
Hoop tight, stave true. Everything else is gossip.
Ale wants oak. Fish wants salt. Both want me.
Knock on the barrel. Hear that? That's honesty.
Leaky? Take it up with the brewer.
Wood remembers what it held. Don't ask what.
morning: Shaves staves with a drawknife in long, curling strokes.
Steams a barrel to bend its belly.
Sorts staves by grain and sets the best aside.
midday: Hammers hoops down with the rhythm of a heartbeat.
Tests a finished cask with water, narrowing his eyes.
Drives the last hoop down and listens for the ring.
evening: Stacks the day's casks against the wall.
Sweeps shavings into a heap for the baker's fire.
Rolls the day's casks into a neat line.
night: Sleeps among barrels, dreaming he's a cask.
Taps one gently on his way to bed, and listens.
Hangs the drawknife on its nail and rests his hands.

tanner.label: Tanner
bark: Leather! Smells like money, stains like sin.
Hides in, boots out, nose never recovers.
Ask me nothing about the pits. I'll tell you everything.
Good leather needs patience and an ugly smell.
Your boots were a cow's idea first.
Don't stand upwind. Stand elsewhere.
morning: Scrapes a hide on a beam, face carefully blank.
Hangs the morning's work to dry, upwind of everyone.
Opens the pit lid and turns his face away.
midday: Stirs the tanning pit with a pole and a martyr's face.
Cuts a strap and tests it between clenched teeth.
Rubs oil into a strap until it shines.
evening: Washes his hands six times and still smells of work.
Sells a belt to a hero, haggling by principle.
Hangs the last hides to drip and walks upwind home.
night: Sleeps outside the town gate, for everyone's sake.
Counts hides by moonlight, mourning each one.
Scrubs his arms to the elbow and sits apart from the fire.

stabler.label: Stabler
bark: Hay, water, a warm stall. The horse pays, the rider complains.
Never stand behind a horse that likes you.
Cavalry horses - proud. Cart horses - wise.
Bridles, saddles, mended. No credit for dead horses.
This one bites. The others merely want to.
A good stable smells of honest work and dishonest horses.
morning: Mucks the stalls with a pitchfork, whistling to the mares.
Fills the water trough and counts noses.
Forks fresh straw into the stalls and checks each hoof.
midday: Brushes a destrier and whispers to it, as to a child.
Shoes a horse with the smith, trading insults.
Rubs liniment on a lame mare's leg and talks low.
evening: Brings the horses in from the yard, one at a time, by name.
Checks the stall latches against a thieving wind.
Hangs the bridles in their order on the wall.
night: Sleeps in the loft, one ear tuned to hooves.
Sings a low lullaby to a nervous colt.
Leans on a stall door with the lamp low and watches the horses settle.

scribe.label: Scribe
bark: Writs, deeds, letters - I write what you meant to say.
Ink is cheaper than a sword and does more damage.
Sign it before the ink dries, or the lawyer will.
Every name in Bellmire passes through my hands, and not all of them are spelled right.
Hush, I'm remembering something.
Legends are drafts until I copy them fair.
morning: Cuts a quill and mixes fresh ink with a sigh.
Sits at the high desk, squinting at yesterday's ledger.
Rules the page with a lead point and straightens his back.
midday: Copies a decree in an elegant hand, tongue between teeth.
Takes a hero's dictation and corrects the grammar.
Reads his own line aloud and strikes out a word.
evening: Sands the day's pages and blows the dust away.
Packs his quills and counts the ink stains on his cuffs.
Closes the ink pot and wipes the nib on a rag.
night: Writes the Chronicle by a single, steady candle.
Dips his quill one more time, just to finish the thought.
Covers the unfinished page and weighs the corners down.

glassblower.label: Glassblower
bark: Glass! Fragile as a promise, twice as costly!
Breathe in, breathe out, the whole trade is breath.
Window panes for the proud. Bottles for the rest.
Careful - it was a vase a moment ago.
A flask of mine holds three brews and one regret.
Heat and patience. Mostly heat.
morning: Fires the furnace to a roar and checks the blowpipe.
Gathers a glowing gob of glass on the end of an iron rod.
Lays out the pipes and rods in the order he will need them.
midday: Blows a bubble, turns it, shapes it, lifts it to the window light.
Cracks a flawed flask, and starts again without complaint.
Turns a hot vessel in the light and lets it be.
evening: Cools the day's work on a rack and counts each piece.
Wraps a finished bottle in straw, with the care of a mother.
Sweeps the cullet into the bin to be melted again.
night: Banks the furnace and sits beside it, face aglow.
Polishes a single lens, humming in dim light.
Watches the annealing oven fade and does not leave it.

wallwright.label: Wallwright
bark: The First Wall stands because I say it does.
Stone on stone, oath on oath. Not a gap tonight.
Raiders hate corners. Build corners.
Check the gate hinges. Check them again. Then pray.
If a crack shows, I'm told. Immediately. Loudly.
A good wall is an argument the enemy cannot win.
morning: Walks the wall-top at dawn, tapping stones with a mallet.
Inspects the gate and its great, groaning hinges.
Checks the plumb of the new course against the old.
midday: Oversees a crew raising a tower, shouting numbers.
Peers at a hairline crack and begins to sweat.
Steps back from the scaffold and counts the stones in the row.
evening: Marks the day's repairs in a battered notebook.
Stands at the gate and watches the road with a builder's pride.
Rolls up the drawings and ties them with a cord.
night: Does the night round, torch in hand, knuckles on stone.
Sleeps in the gatehouse with the wall at his back.
Walks the wall-top once more and stops at a stone he trusts.

crier.label: Crier
bark: Hear ye! Bellmire stands another day!
Grain counted, flasks measured, door kept!
News from the guild, news from the Ford, news from nobody in particular!
Heroes fall, heroes rise, the Chronicle writes all!
Market opens! Market closes! Market, in short, exists!
The bell has no clapper - so I must be louder!
morning: Clears his throat on the Market Cross like a man about to fight a goose.
Rehearses the morning proclamations in a whisper.
Warms his voice on a low note and tests the Cross.
midday: Bellows the news from the Market Cross to an unimpressed crowd.
Rings a hand-bell and recites the day's prices at speed.
Reads the guild price list twice to be sure of the numbers.
evening: Calls out the closing of the market, voice cracked and proud.
Reads the guild notices to a handful of listeners.
Folds the day's notices and hands the bell to the boy.
night: Sits on the cross steps, sipping honey-water for his throat.
Mutters the next day's news until he forgets it.
Says the town's name out loud, quietly, to nobody.

guardsman.label: Guardsman
bark: Halt! State your business. State it quickly.
The Commander sees all. The Commander sees me, now stand straight.
Gate's open till dusk. After that, knock politely.
Nothing to report. Nothing is how I like it.
Raiders come at dawn, mostly. They're early risers too.
Stay behind the line, citizen. The line is there for a reason.
morning: Takes the morning watch with a yawn and a spear.
Polishes his helm and finds it dull anyway.
Checks the gate bar and the watch-fire.
midday: Stands at the gate, face stern, stomach complaining.
Drills with the Commander's voice cracking like a whip.
Counts the carts through the gate and says the number aloud.
evening: Hands the watch to the night guard, grumbling.
Shares a stew with the gate crew, swapping tall stories.
Eats his bread standing, spear against the wall.
night: Walks the dark wall with a lantern and a frown.
Sits in the gatehouse, listening to the Ford murmur.
Looks down the road a long time and sees nothing, which is the job.

bellkeeper.label: Bell-Keeper
bark: The bell has no clapper. Do not tell it. It has feelings.
I wind nothing, I oil nothing, I keep it anyway.
It rings in the quiet places. You'll know when.
Every town has a bell. Ours remembers.
Ask the bell. It won't answer. That's why it's wise.
Keep the door, keep the bell. The rest takes care of itself.
morning: Climbs the tower to look at a bell that cannot ring.
Dusts the bell's lip with a feather and a sigh.
Opens the shutters in the tower to let the morning in.
midday: Sits beneath the bell with a book, never reading it.
Answers a child's question about the clapper with a long, sad story.
Oils the hinge on the door under the bell.
evening: Sweeps the tower stair with ceremony.
Looks up at the bell as the sun sets, nodding at some private joke.
Winds the lamp up the rope and trims it for the night.
night: Stands very still below the bell, listening.
Locks the tower and leaves a candle in the window.
Sits one step below the bell and says nothing for an hour.

raid: Raiders! Get the children inside - my bread can burn, they can't!
Not the oven! Take the silver, leave the oven!
Bar the door! Bar it again! Is that barred? Bar it!
The Commander's at the gate. We'll be fine. We'll be fine. Won't we?
My boy's on the wall. Gods, let him keep his head down.
They always come when the dough is rising. Always.
Grab the ledger! The ledger, you fool, not the cat!
I've seen three raids. This one smells worse.
Shutters down! Water buckets up! Nobody be a hero!
If they break the gate I'm hiding in the barrel. The cooper knows.
Keep the lamps low and the voices lower!
They took half my stock last time. This time I'm armed with a ladle.
Is it over? It's over? Don't lie to me.
The wall held. Thank the wallwright. Thank anyone.
Count the children. Count them twice. Then count the sheep.
Smoke on the ridge - they're coming round the east side!
Hold the line, neighbours! Our roofs, our rules!
My knees say run. My pride says stay. Pride is losing.
Take the cart and go! I'll mind the shop!
Not today, you thieving sods. Not in Bellmire.
disaster: It's the end! No - it's weather. It's only weather. Probably.
Move the grain! Higher! Higher still!
My roof's gone! My roof is simply gone!
The marsh has risen again, and the cat with it.
Everyone to the chapel! It has stone walls and a door!
Water's in the cellar. The ale! The ALE!
Pray if you've got the breath. Dig if you've got the arms.
I've lived here twenty years. Never seen a sky that colour.
Bring blankets! Bring bread! Bring anything that isn't wet!
The Ford's swallowed the ferry. The ferryman is furious.
Get the herds in! Get the herds in before they get ideas!
The scar's humming. It's never done that before.
Stay together and keep the lamps lit!
Will the wall hold the water? Will the water hold the wall?
It'll pass. Everything passes, except the bill.
My field! Look at my field!
Cover the well! Cover the well and save the sweet water!
The old folk said it would come. The old folk say everything.
If the sky wants war, the sky can have a queue.
We'll rebuild. We always rebuild. It's the Bellmire way, and the Bellmire curse.
Bar the shutters. Then bar them again.
Water in the cellar. Water in the loft. Water in the soup.
Roof's off the byre. The cow's in the kitchen.
Keep the lamps low and the children close.
It'll pass. They always pass. Hold the rope.
The reed-cutters say it's the worst in years. They say that every year.
Mud to the doorstep. I'll sweep it Tuesday.
Hands to the sandbags. Gossip after.
The bell's cracked. Nobody heard it anyway.
We lost the fence. We kept the pig.
festival: Ale's on the house! Well - on the brewer, but he agreed!
Dance, you lumps! The day won't last!
Look at the lanterns! Aren't they fine?
Bread for all and a song for none - the bard's on strike!
A holiday! The first in a fortnight!
Mind the bonfire, children. And the bard. Both bite.
Come join the dance! Your wife already did. Your wife's very good.
Who brought the honey cakes? Marry me. Marry me now.
My feet hurt. My heart sings. A fair trade.
The Commander's smiling. It's frightening, but welcome.
No raids, no floods, no taxes - say it with me!
I'll sleep in tomorrow. Tomorrow's a promise.
A toast to the Ford, and the wall, and the clapperless bell!
Smell that roast? Don't ask where the pig came from.
Bellmire stands, and tonight she dances.
Pour another. The cellar's deep and the worries shallow.
Hang the garlands high. The wind will do the rest.
Even the guards are singing. Badly, but singing.
A good day, neighbours. Remember it when the grey comes back.
One more dance, then the dishes. Promise.
caravan: Wagons! Wagons on the road! Open the gate!
What did they bring? Salt? Spice? Hope?
Mind the prices - they know we need it.
About time. My shelves are bare as a monk's purse.
Look at that silk! Look at the price! Look away!
The merchants smile as they take our coin. I smile as I haggle.
Grain! Real grain! The old sacks were mostly dust.
Iron at last. Smith's been sulking for a month.
They brought news from the south. None of it is good. All of it is interesting.
Bring the carts round! Unload before the rain!
Hide your daughters, the drovers are in town. No, hide your purses.
Spices for the stew pot! The Ford has flavour at last.
Count what they brought. Then count what they took.
A fair deal, a fair day, a fair road home to them.
Oil for the lamps! Light for the winter!
They say the road is bad. They say it every time.
Bellmire's on the map now - look, a caravan.
If they've brought dye, I'm closing the shop and weeping.
The guild clerk will want every sack inked.
Welcome, strangers! Spend freely and leave gently.
growth: The wall's grown again. Lord, we're becoming something.
More houses. More neighbours. More complaints.
A new well, a new street - I'll need a new map.
Bellmire's no crossing any more. Say it with pride.
The market's wider! So are the queues.
They say we're a town now. I still feel like a hut.
New faces every week. I can't remember the old ones.
Rooms above the shop! Finally, a place to sleep.
They've raised the First Wall. I weep, I cheer, I pay the tax.
Another guildsman arrived. The smith nearly wept.
Business is good. Don't tell the guild, they'll raise the fee.
My grandmother wouldn't know the place. Neither do I.
The streets have names now. Mine is Muddy Lane.
We outgrew the old well. And the old ways. And the old boots.
More folk means more trade, more noise, more thieves, more of everything.
A day's walk, and you can see the walls from the road!
Bellmire, a city one day. I'll still sell the same loaves.
The masons are singing. Listen - they're singing!
Growth is good. Growing pains are cheaper than shrinking.
Stand tall, Bellmire. You're getting taller.
hunger: The bin's empty. The bin was full yesterday.
Measure the grain, count the flasks, keep the door - and ration the lot.
I gave the heel of the loaf to the child. I'm fine.
My belly's louder than the bell. And the bell has no clapper.
Rations! Half rations! Quarter rations?
No bread today. Don't ask. I'll cry.
The fish have fled. The fishwife glares at the river.
