I'd trade a sword for a sack of oats.
The stew's mostly water. The water's mostly mud.
Hunger's no dragon, but it breathes just as hot.
Who's hoarding grain? Don't look at me. Look at the miller.
Chew slowly. It tricks the stomach.
The herd's thin. The harvest's thinner.
We held the wall. Can't we hold the pantry?
Who saw the caravan? Where's the caravan?
A turnip is a feast tonight.
Pull the belts tight and the neighbours tighter.
We'll eat. We always eat. Eventually.
My daughter asked for cake. I told her the cake was on holiday.
The scar's greedy. So is winter.
Half a loaf. Cut it thin.
The pot's on. Nothing's in it. It's warm, though.
Ask the baker. The baker's asking the miller.
We counted the sacks twice. They did not grow.
Eat slow. Talk less.
The child's quiet. That worries me more than the crying.
Last of the cheese went to the guards.
The well's fine. The larder's not.
I'd cross the marsh for an onion.
Soup again. Thinner soup.
hero_falls: Another hero down. The chapel keeper's already sweeping.
Poor lad. He bought a round last week.
We'll dig the plot by dawn. The gravedigger won't charge.
They go so bravely and come back so rarely.
Say a word, neighbours. The Chronicle can't say it all.
Light a candle. Not for him - for his mother.
He owed me three coppers. I forgive them. Truly.
The dungeon takes what it takes.
I thought they were invincible. Silly of me.
Another name for the wall of the fallen.
It's quiet in the tavern tonight.
Gods keep him. Gods and the grave-lanterns.
Wasn't he the one with the lute? He was.
I'll miss the way she swore at the stairs.
Remember him as he went: grinning.
Even the guards took their helms off.
Who'll tell his family? Somebody has to.
A hero's death is a short story. A hero's life, a long one.
Bury him with his boots. He'd want that.
Bellmire remembers. That's what we do.
hero_rich: Look at him! Pockets full, boots shining!
Spend it in Bellmire, love - and spend it fast!
Another delver rich. Another round on his tab.
He's come home laden like a mule. Good mule.
Clear the table - a hero with silver wants a seat!
Coin to the smith, coin to the tailor, coin to me.
Don't flaunt it. The raiders have ears.
If he's buying, I'm drinking.
He left a poor man and returned a lord. Lords drink more.
The innkeeper's already polishing the best tankard.
Look at the gem! Look at the size! Don't touch.
Delvers get rich. Townsfolk get richer.
That's the trouble with heroes: they're generous.
I'll sell him a hat. Then another. He can wear both.
The Chronicle will write this one up. The coin, not the man.
Treasure! And not a scratch on him. Suspicious.
Come, sit, tell us everything - and leave the purse on the bar.
Wealth's a fine thing till it's your neighbour's.
Rich now, dead tomorrow. Drink up, friend.
The guild clerk's smiling. Never trust a smiling clerk.

lines: Second flood this season. The river's learned the way to my door.
Twice in one season. The marsh is courting us, and badly.
Another fire. Another bucket line. Another bad week for thatch.
Second blaze this season. Someone's been careless, or the sky has.
Dry again. The well-keeper's started talking to the bucket.
Second drought this season. The crops have given up apologising.
Cold snap twice in a season. Winter's moved in without asking.
The frost came back for its hat. And my pipes.
Second blight this season. The turnips have started leaving notes.
Same black rot as before. We'd mourn it, but the mourning cost more.
Sickness again. The apothecary's out of sage and patience.
Twice sick in a season. Even the chapel keeper's coughing.
The scarstorm again. That scar has a temper.
Second scarstorm. My spoons are humming.
Another quake. The wallwright's started praying to the foundations.
Ground's shaken twice now. The mason says it's showing off.
Three disasters in a row. Either we're cursed or we're dull.
Flood, fire, famine - the gods are working through a list.
Ten raids we've weathered. The wall has more scars than I do.
Ten raids, and Bellmire still stands. Stubborn, aren't we?
Twenty-five raids. I've stopped flinching. I haven't stopped swearing.
The old gate's seen twenty-five raids. It deserves a medal.
Three raids running. They're getting bold - and so are we.
Third raid this week. My nerves have retired.
Quiet five days now. I don't trust it.
Peace for five days. The Commander's worried. That's how I know.
Twelve days of peace. The children are learning to be bored.
Nothing for a fortnight, near enough. Even the guards have run out of gossip.
We grew too fast. The larder didn't get the memo.
More mouths, same loaf. Growth tastes thin.
After the flood, a feast. It tastes better, I'll say that.
We danced on the ashes, and the ashes didn't mind.
We drink to the wall because the wall drank first.
The dancing's wilder after a raid. Nobody counts the stumbles.
That's two heroes this week. The gravedigger's asked for a raise.
Another hero down. The chapel keeper's run out of candles.
He came back! The same one we buried? No - another. It's confusing.
Last week we mourned her. Today she's on the ale bench. Bellmire!
No caravan this month. The merchants have forgotten us.
The road's empty. The smith has taken to stroking his anvil.
The caravan! Right when the bin was bare. I could kiss the oxen.
Grain on the road at last. Never been so pleased to see a merchant.
A town now. And yet my hens still look at me like I'm a hut.
Walls grew. Folk grew. The mud, alas, grows too.
The Commander's in barracks. Don't worry. He never dies. He only sulks.
E3PO's resting. He'll be back, louder than ever.
The Commander's back on the wall. I feel taller.
Back at his post, and not a scratch left. I'd swear he'd lie.

cast.name: Maud Reedwhistle
cast.bio: Widow of a ferryman who never came back from the Ford. Sells fish, sells opinions, and buys neither.
bark: Trout, three coppers, and a free word of warning.
Eels! Slippery as a clerk!
My husband's river, my husband's fish. I just sell them.
Don't haggle with a woman who gutted a pike this morning.
cast.morning: Maud gutting trout on the landing stones, gulls already waiting.
cast.midday: Maud shouting the day's catch to the market, voice like a rusty hinge.
cast.evening: Maud scrubbing her knife in the river, humming her husband's song.
cast.night: Maud smoking the last eels over a low fire, whispering to the smoke.

react.raid: Maud grabs her knife and her children. 'Come on, we've gutted worse than raiders.'
react.disaster: Maud eyes the river. 'It's taken one man from me. It'll not take the stall.'
react.festival: Maud sells the last of her pike and dances once, badly, with a sack of salt.
react.caravan: Maud eyes the wagons. 'Salt. At last. My fish and I are saved.'
react.growth: Maud counts the new houses. 'More mouths. More fish. More river to blame.'
react.hunger: Maud gives her own bread to a child. 'I'm not hungry. I'm cold. Different thing.'
react.hero_falls: Maud lights a candle by her stall. 'The river took the ferryman. The dungeon takes heroes. Same hunger.'
react.hero_rich: Maud sniffs. 'Rich, is he? Buy a trout, hero. You owe the river.'

lines: Maud, on the second flood: 'The river's pining for him. I can hear it from the stall.'
Maud, after ten raids: 'Ten times they came. Ten times my knife stayed sharp.'

cast.name: Tobyn Ironside
cast.bio: Bellmire's smith, huge and soft-spoken. Mended the Commander's helm four times and has never once been thanked.
bark: Hit it hot, hit it true, hit it again.
Don't touch the anvil. It's heavy and I'm proud.
Nails, hinges, hooks - small iron, big town.
The scar eats spells. It tastes of nothing on steel.
cast.morning: Tobyn raking the forge awake, soot to his elbows.
cast.midday: Tobyn hammering at a glowing bar, ears long since ruined.
cast.evening: Tobyn quenching a blade, the hiss like a slow snake.
cast.night: Tobyn banking the forge, humming a song about iron.

react.raid: Tobyn lifts the biggest hammer. 'Over my anvil, lads.'
react.disaster: Tobyn shuts the forge and prays to iron. 'Hold, anvil. Hold.'
react.festival: Tobyn nurses a mug. 'Tomorrow I'll hammer. Tonight I'm a lamb.'
react.caravan: Tobyn eyes the ore. 'Finally. Real iron. Not that gravel from before.'
react.growth: Tobyn grins at the new smithy. 'Room for two anvils. Room for two arguments.'
react.hunger: Tobyn eats cold porridge. 'Metal doesn't need food. I do. Tragic.'
react.hero_falls: Tobyn sets down a hammer. 'I've mended his armour. I couldn't mend him.'
react.hero_rich: Tobyn winks. 'Rich hero? Good. My tongs need replacing.'

lines: Tobyn, on the second fire: 'Twice in a season. The forge feels slighted.'
Tobyn, after ten raids: 'Ten times I've sharpened the guard's spears. They bring them back dull.'

cast.name: Elspeth Hartley
cast.bio: Keeper of the chapel and the list of the fallen. Reads every name aloud, every morning, whether or not anyone listens.
bark: The bell has no clapper and still it speaks.
cast.morning: Elspeth sweeping the chapel floor and reading yesterday's names.
cast.midday: Elspeth hearing a confession in the doorway, hand on a nervous shoulder.
cast.evening: Elspeth closing the shutters against the evening wind.
cast.night: Elspeth keeping vigil by one candle, speaking to no one.

react.raid: Elspeth locks the chapel door. 'Inside, all of you. Gods are less picky than raiders.'
react.disaster: Elspeth lifts the candle. 'Pray if you have breath. Dig if you have arms.'
react.festival: Elspeth smiles. 'Dance, my dears. The dead would want it, I think.'
react.caravan: Elspeth nods at the wagons. 'Candles. Oil. Linen. Bless the road.'
react.growth: Elspeth touches a new stone. 'Another course. Another name to carve one day.'
react.hunger: Elspeth gives out bread. 'No sermon today. The bread is the sermon.'
react.hero_falls: Elspeth writes a name in the book, slow. 'I know this one. He laughed at the door.'
react.hero_rich: Elspeth lifts an eyebrow. 'Wealth is a gift. The giving back is the sermon.'

lines: Elspeth, on the second flood: 'Water is patient. The chapel is more so.'
Elspeth, after ten raids: 'We've buried fewer than I feared. I thank the wall, and the Commander.'

cast.name: Bram Barrelbelly
cast.bio: Brewer of the thickest ale in the valley. Tastes every batch, swears he doesn't, and has not seen his own feet in years.
bark: Ale! Thick enough to chew, strong enough to forget!
cast.morning: Bram stirring the mash with a paddle taller than a child.
cast.midday: Bram rolling casks to the cart, grunting rhythm.
cast.evening: Bram pouring the first round at the tavern, thick fingers around the tankard.
cast.night: Bram snoring in the brewhouse, nose full of yeast and ambition.

react.raid: Bram hauls a cask to the gate. 'Roll it at them! Ale is heavy!'
react.disaster: Bram clutches a barrel. 'My ale! My precious ale! Higher, higher!'
react.festival: Bram bows to the crowd. 'Free round! It's on the house. Mine. I'm the house.'
react.caravan: Bram sniffs the wagons. 'Hops! Real hops! I'll weep, I swear it.'
react.growth: Bram slaps the new brewhouse wall. 'Bigger vats, bigger belly, bigger Bram.'
react.hunger: Bram stares at the empty vat. 'I've never wanted water before. Now I do.'
react.hero_falls: Bram lifts a tankard to the sky. 'To the empty chair. May he never run dry.'
react.hero_rich: Bram laughs. 'Rich? Good! He can pay his tab.'

lines: Bram, on the second flood: 'Twice in a season, and the cellar still floats my ale. Hah!'
Bram, after ten raids: 'Ten raids. My vats are the best-defended place in town.'

cast.name: Nell Candlemas
cast.bio: Bellmire's baker, up before dawn since she was twelve. Gives the burnt loaves to anyone who looks hungry and the good ones to anyone who looks rich.
bark: Hot loaves! The bell may have no clapper but my oven rings true!
Bread for the Ford, bread for the road.
cast.morning: Nell firing the oven before dawn, swearing at the flour sack.
cast.midday: Nell sliding loaves from the peel, face red as the coals.
cast.evening: Nell sweeping the oven floor, counting the unsold.
cast.night: Nell banking the coals and setting the dough to rise.

react.raid: Nell flings a loaf at a raider. 'That's a day's bread, you thief!'
react.disaster: Nell stacks her loaves high. 'Shelf them! Shelf them! Nothing wet!'
react.festival: Nell dusts off her apron. 'Honey cakes for everyone. One each. One!'
react.caravan: Nell eyes the sacks. 'Flour! Beautiful, dusty flour!'
react.growth: Nell counts new customers. 'More ovens, more mouths, more me.'
react.hunger: Nell halves each loaf. 'Chew slow. It tricks the belly.'
react.hero_falls: Nell wipes a tear with a floury sleeve. 'He liked the heel. Always the heel.'
react.hero_rich: Nell hums. 'Rich, is he? Then he'll buy the whole batch. Won't he?'

lines: Nell, on the second flood: 'Dough doesn't rise in a wet cellar. I've tested it.'
Nell, after ten raids: 'Ten raids and my oven's never gone cold. That's grit.'

cast.name: Wat Mudboot
cast.bio: Gravedigger. Cheerful in the way of men who have seen everything and still enjoy a pie. Talks to the graves; the graves have never complained.
bark: One more for the plot. Sorry, one more for the pile.
cast.morning: Wat marking out a fresh plot with string and a surly look.
cast.midday: Wat eating his lunch on a headstone, apologising to it.
cast.evening: Wat cleaning his boots at the chapel gate, nodding to the dead.
cast.night: Wat sitting among the stones, telling them the day's news.

react.raid: Wat shoulders his spade. 'Not today, raiders. Not here. I've paperwork.'
react.disaster: Wat leans on the spade. 'Wet earth, dry jokes. A good day for it.'
react.festival: Wat sits on a grave and watches the dancing. 'They'd approve. Mostly.'
react.caravan: Wat leans on his spade. 'Wagons! More folk, eventually more work. Sorry.'
react.growth: Wat grins at the new street. 'More folk, more customers. Eventually. Sorry.'
react.hunger: Wat shrugs. 'Hunger's good for business. Which I regret saying aloud.'
react.hero_falls: Wat pats the fresh mound. 'Rest well, lad. I did it nicely.'
react.hero_rich: Wat tips his cap. 'Rich hero? I'll dig him a deeper hole. Just in case.'

lines: Wat, on the second flood: 'Water in the graves. I'll not say what I think of that.'
Wat, after ten raids: 'Ten raids, and I buried fewer than I feared. Pity for business, joy for town.'

cast.name: Sibyl Wickham
cast.bio: Apothecary whose remedies mostly work, and whose bills always do. Keeps a green bottle on the top shelf that she has never been seen to open.
bark: The green bottle is not for sale. Stop asking.
Fever, flux, or foolishness - I treat all three.
cast.morning: Sibyl grinding herbs in a mortar the size of a head.
cast.midday: Sibyl measuring drops with a trembling, practised spoon.
cast.evening: Sibyl corking bottles and wiping the counter.
cast.night: Sibyl brewing by candlelight, whispering rhymes to the pot.

react.raid: Sibyl slams the shutters. 'Bandages are at the back, children first!'
react.disaster: Sibyl pulls out her good flasks. 'It'll be wet and sore tonight. Line up.'
react.festival: Sibyl sips a cup. 'Medicinal. I'm entirely medicinal.'
react.caravan: Sibyl eyes the crates. 'Sage! Valerian! Bless the road.'
react.growth: Sibyl counts the new rooms. 'More folk, more coughs.'
react.hunger: Sibyl rations the honey. 'Half a spoon each. Medicinal. Don't argue.'
react.hero_falls: Sibyl lowers her voice. 'There was nothing in the bottle. That's what makes it hard.'
react.hero_rich: Sibyl smiles. 'Rich? Wonderful. Let me sell you something for the nerves.'

lines: Sibyl, on the second sickness: 'I told the Chief it would come back. Do I get thanks? Never.'
Sibyl, after ten raids: 'Ten raids, a hundred bandages. The green bottle remains full.'

cast.name: Godric Fordbright
cast.bio: Guardsman at the gate. Idolises the Commander so thoroughly he salutes the Commander's boots.
bark: The Commander sees all. The Commander sees me. Stand straight.
Stay behind the line, citizen.
cast.morning: Godric taking the morning watch with a yawn and a spear.
cast.midday: Godric standing at the gate, face stern, stomach complaining.
cast.evening: Godric swapping the watch, grumbling about the cold.
cast.night: Godric walking the dark wall with a lantern and a frown.

react.raid: Godric squares up. 'For the Commander! For the Ford! For breakfast!'
react.disaster: Godric shouts orders. 'Citizens to the chapel! Move, move!'
react.festival: Godric straightens his helm. 'Off duty. Mostly. Still watching you.'
react.caravan: Godric checks the wagons with a stern eye. 'Papers. Papers! Hello, lovely.'
react.growth: Godric salutes the new wall. 'Bigger wall, longer watch. Worth it.'
react.hunger: Godric tightens his belt. 'The Commander eats little. So do I.'
react.hero_falls: Godric lowers his spear. 'He fell on the stair. I'll remember.'
react.hero_rich: Godric nods. 'Good for him. Gives us all something to aim at.'

lines: Godric, on the second fire: 'Twice in a season, and the gate's still standing. Gods bless stone.'
Godric, after ten raids: 'Ten raids and not one past me. The Commander noticed. He nodded.'

cast.name: Hob Coldfingers
cast.bio: Reed-cutter who knows every pool of the marsh by sound alone. Distrusts anyone who walks the soft ground confidently.
bark: The marsh hums if you stand quiet.
cast.morning: Hob wading out at first light with a hooked knife and a bad back.
cast.midday: Hob binding bundles with a speed that shames the guild clerks.
cast.evening: Hob smearing mud on his neck against the midges.
cast.night: Hob listening to the marsh from his doorstep, one boot off.

react.raid: Hob slips into the reeds. 'They'll never find me. I'm marsh.'
react.disaster: Hob eyes the water. 'It's coming up. Ask the frogs. They agree.'
react.festival: Hob taps a reed like a pipe. 'A tune, a tune, for the lads!'
react.caravan: Hob counts the wagons. 'They'll buy my thatch. Eventually. Everyone does.'
react.growth: Hob squints at the houses. 'More thatch, more reed. Good for me. Good for the frogs.'
react.hunger: Hob chews a stalk. 'Reed is bitter. Hunger is worse.'
react.hero_falls: Hob wipes his knife. 'The marsh kept him. I hope it's kind.'
react.hero_rich: Hob snorts. 'Rich? Let him buy thatch. The roof is his future.'

lines: Hob, on the second flood: 'The water knows my name. I'd rather it forgot.'
Hob, after ten raids: 'Ten raids, and none found my hut. That's craft.'

cast.name: Agnes Gatewood
cast.bio: Innkeeper of the only inn that matters. Has heard every hero's boast and settled every hero's tab, usually twice.
bark: The stew has a name. I won't tell you what it is.
Tab's on the slate. The slate remembers.
cast.morning: Agnes changing the straw and sweeping up what the night left.
cast.midday: Agnes ladling stew for a table of hungry delvers.
cast.evening: Agnes filling the room with noise, steam and a bard who can't sing.
cast.night: Agnes locking the cellar and sleeping with the keys under her pillow.

react.raid: Agnes bars the inn door. 'Everyone upstairs! I'm charging double for the safety.'
react.disaster: Agnes stacks the ale high. 'Cellar's flooding. Drink it first!'
react.festival: Agnes tops every cup. 'Tonight I'm generous. Tomorrow, I'm Agnes.'
react.caravan: Agnes counts barrels with greedy eyes. 'Wine! Spice! Now we're a proper inn.'
react.growth: Agnes admires a new wing. 'More beds, more coin, more complaints.'
react.hunger: Agnes stirs a thin stew. 'It's mostly stew. Today it's mostly water.'
react.hero_falls: Agnes pours one for the empty seat. 'On the house. He'd never have paid it.'
react.hero_rich: Agnes grins. 'Rich hero? Best room. Best price. Best behaviour.'

lines: Agnes, on the second flood: 'My cellar's a pond. My drinkers are fish.'
Agnes, after ten raids: 'Ten raids, and nobody's broken a window I couldn't bill.'

festivals._note: C-49 / WORK_PLAN C6 - THE FESTIVAL HAS A VOICE. D63 reads these instead of town.gd's two hardcoded lines. Dead until wired; content worker never touches code. Additive. KEY SHAPE: reasons{harvest,raid_survived,lord_felled,hero_home,town_level,viewer_gift}[] -> the OPENING line, pick by the reason that triggered the festival; crowd[] -> ambient shout from any townsperson during it; toasts[] -> raised-cup lines; stalls[] -> what the stalls are selling (a ticker or a stall sign); notables[] -> {who,line} a named notable's line (who matches townsfolk.cast name); e3po[] -> the Commander's festival line (E3PO cannot die and never leaves his post); closings[] -> end-of-festival lines. viewer_paid{...} is a separate richer set for a festival a VIEWER paid for: every string there may carry the token {buyer} (the paying viewer's display name) - substitute it, or strip it with its comma if the name is unknown. Cost statement: a viewer festival is purchased with bits/points by the buyer; the lines promise nothing mechanical beyond 'the town celebrates'. No floor counts.

harvest: The last cart is in. Bellmire holds its Harvest Feast.
Grain counted, barns full. Light the long tables.
The reed-cutters and the millers call it: Harvest Feast tonight.
The scythes are hung up. The ale is not.
A good year in the field. The crier orders a feast.
Sacks to the rafters. Bellmire eats before it counts.
Harvest is home. The ovens have been lit since dawn.
Gold fields, full bellies. Feast on the green.
The mill ran dry of corn to grind. Time to eat what it ground.
The last sheaf is bound with a ribbon. The feast begins.
Even the crows are fat. Bellmire holds its Harvest Feast.
Bring a bowl and a stool - the harvest was kind this year.
Last sheaf in. The crier names a Harvest Feast.
The barns are full and the tally agrees. Tables out.
Straw on the road, grain in the loft. Feast tonight.
The millers ran late and finished. Harvest Feast.
A good year on the long field. Bring your own bowl.
Nobody was short at the count. That earns a feast.
The reed-cutters are home dry. Harvest Feast at dusk.
Cart after cart till dark. The crier calls the feast.
raid_survived: The walls held. Bellmire feasts the night it lived.
Bandits broken at the gate. Pour for the wall-walkers.
The raid is over and nobody left the count. Feast!
Smoke clears, the bell rings once, and the tables come out.
We were not taken. That is worth a festival.
The gate stands and so do we. Light the lanterns.
The raiders fled the Ford. The town dances on their tracks.
Wounds bound, shields stacked. Bellmire calls a Victory Night.
Survived is a fine reason. The crier declares a feast.
The guard held the line. The town returns the favour in ale.
Not a door lost, not a soul lost. Mark it: Gate-Holding Day.
The raid broke on the wall like surf. Now the tables go up.
The wall stood. The town eats on it.
Raiders gone by dawn. Pour for the watch.
Gate barred, count taken, nobody missing. Feast.
They came at night. We kept the door. Feast.
The wall-walkers are hoarse and whole. Feast tonight.
Carts hauled the broken ladders off. Light the fires.
The count came out right. That is worth a feast.
Bellmire held, and Bellmire is hungry.
lord_felled: A dungeon lord is dead. Bellmire hangs the banners.
The scar is quieter tonight. The crier calls a Felling Feast.
A lord is down and the guild bell will not stop ringing.
They carried the proof up the stairs. The town will not sleep.
The lord that frightened the Ford is finished. Drink to it.
One less shadow under the hill. The lanterns go up.
The delvers did it. The town pays in meat and music.
The scar owes us one lord. We call it a feast.
A lord's crown on the guild table. Come see, come eat.
They said it could not be felled. Bellmire raises a cup to the liars.
The ground will not forget, but tonight it can be quiet. Feast.
Tell the children: a lord died. Then let them have cake.
A lord is dead. The guild bell rings it twice.
The scar is lighter by one. Felling Feast.
Word came up from the dark: it is done. Feast.
A lord fell below. Hang the banners.
Something old stopped breathing today. Bellmire pours.
The crier read the name and then the date. Feast.
One less under the town. Tables out.
The lord is down. The hero is up. Feast.
hero_home: A hero walks in from the scar. The town turns out.
Home from the dark, alive. That is a festival all by itself.
The gate opens on a face we feared lost. Fetch the fiddlers.
Bellmire welcomes its delver home. Hang the lanterns low.
They went down and they came back. Pour the good ale.
Mud to the knee and grinning: a hero is home. Feast!
The bell rings for one name tonight. Make way.
A delver returns with a full pack and a story. Clear a table.
The scar gave one back. Bellmire says thank you loudly.
Home again. The innkeeper has already set a place.
Another one comes up the stairs breathing. Celebrate it.
The road in is lined with townsfolk. A hero is home.
The hero is up out of the dark. Open the gate.
Lamp still lit, boots still on. Home feast.
They counted heads at the gate. One more than feared.
Back from the scar and walking. Fetch the bread.
The gate-keeper saw the lamp first. The town followed.
A hero came home. That is the whole reason.
Mud to the knee and smiling. Feast.
Up the stair and out. The crier calls a feast.
town_level: Bellmire has grown a stage. The crier declares a Raising Day.
New roofs, new roads. The town throws itself a party.
A bigger Bellmire needs a bigger celebration. Tables out!
The town has outgrown its old name's pride. Feast the new walls.
Another rung up the long climb. Ring the bell twice.
The builders are paid and the rafters are up. Raise a cup.
Look how far the huts have come. Festival!
Growth has a taste, and tonight it is honey cake.
Bellmire is more than it was this morning. Mark the day.
The mason's stone is set. Come eat beneath it.
A new stage, a new banner. The crier is hoarse already.
The town stands taller. Let the music stand taller still.
New timber on the hill. Raising Day.
Bellmire is a bigger town since morning. Feast.
The mason signed the last wall. Raising Day.
More roofs than last week. The crier counts them aloud.
The road is paved a stage further. Tables out.
A grown town owes itself a meal. Raising Day.
The new stage is up and holding. Light the lamps.
Stone where there was timber. Feast.
viewer_gift: A gift has come to Bellmire. The crier names a feast.
Someone far away sent a kindness. The town pays it forward.
A gift from the watchers! Light the lanterns.
The strongbox rattles with a stranger's generosity. Feast!
Word from beyond the Ford: a gift for the town. Tables out.
A kind hand reached in from the dark. Bellmire answers in song.
A gift lands on the green and the whole town hears it clink.
Generosity, unannounced. The crier makes it a festival.
The guild treasurer weeps, then orders a barrel.
A gift, and no ask attached. Bellmire does not forget that.
Someone remembered Bellmire. Bellmire remembers back.
A gift for the town. The innkeeper tallies it in ale.
Someone paid for a feast. The crier says thanks.
A gift from afar. Bellmire sets the tables.
The watchers sent kindness. We send it back as bread.
Coin came in with a kind word. Feast tonight.
Somebody far off remembered us. Light the lanterns.
The crier read the gift out. Nobody said no.
A kindness arrived at the gate. Tables out.
Paid for by a stranger. Eaten by everyone.

crowd: Make room at the long table!
Who stole my turnip tart?
Pass the cider, pass the cider!
Dance, you lumps! The day won't last!
Look at the lanterns! Aren't they fine?
Gate's shut and the cup's full!
Mind my toes, you great ox!
Another round for the wall-walkers!
Fiddler! Something with a stamp in it!
Save me a pie, I'm only going to dance.
Ha! Even the guard is smiling!
Somebody count the barrels. Then don't.
Where did the dog get a sausage?
A ribbon for the brave, a ribbon for the lucky!
Hold the cup, hold the cup, I'm going in!
Bellmire! Bellmire! Bellmire!
My feet are done. My hands are not.
Is that honey cake or is it a miracle?
Careful, the cider has opinions.
One more song and then the chores!
Tell it again, the bit with the goblin!
The little ones have the whole green for a race.
Somebody lend me a hat for the toast.
That fiddler is a wizard, I swear it.
If this is a dream, nobody wake me.
Bread, cheese, and nobody barking orders. Bliss.
Hoist me up, I want to see the lanterns!
Bring the barrel closer, my arm is short.
A kiss for the cook! A coin for the cook!
The reed-cutters are winning the tug-of-war!
Boots off, boots off, the grass is warm.
No raids tonight, say the stars.
Who knows the words to the Ford song?
Cheers to the hearth that kept us!
I will remember this at the bottom of the scar.
Leave the washing. It will wait.
Oh, what a night for it!
Single-file for the pie line, you savages!
Shh! The singing starts.
toasts: To the wall, and the ones who walk it!
To the Ford, may it never run dry!
To the dead, who bought us the morning.
To the delvers: down, and back again!
To Bellmire - small, stubborn, ours!
To the guard, and the guard's bad jokes!
To the hearth, the ale, and the lock on the door!
To the bell: may it ring for joy, not for fear!
To the harvest, and the hands that brought it!
To whoever fixed the roof last night!
To the scar: may it stay quiet and stay down!
To the cook, who made one pot feed everyone!
To the road home, wherever it runs!
To lost friends and found coin!
To full cups and empty graves!
To the ones who stayed and held the gate!
To dawn, and the new day it owes us!
To the mud that made us what we are!
To the long climb. One stage at a time!
To the watchers beyond the Ford - may they never lack for supper!
To the lantern, the candle, and the spark!
To luck - the only guild we all joined!
To the child with the first sword, and the grandmother who hid it!
To the damp, the draught, and the drink that cures both!
To what we built, and to the beams that carry it!
To bread, to blood, to Bellmire!
To the fiddlers who never sleep!
To a quiet night. May it last a week!
To the gate - shut and proud!
To the ones we owe. Everyone!
stalls: Honey cakes, a copper each, and one is a coin in disguise.
Roast pork on a stick. The stick is free.
Cider by the cup, warm, with cloves.
Ribbons for the brave and a ribbon for the unbrave.
Smoked trout from the Ford, still smelling of the river.
Pies - mutton, apple, and 'ask me tomorrow'.
A brewer's barrel, tapped and sweating.
Candied turnip, a Bellmire horror and a Bellmire delight.
Wooden swords for the little ones. Splinters extra.
Fortune-telling: three coppers, no refunds.
Spiced wine, which is only half water.
Flat bread with soft cheese and a handful of herbs.
A ring toss. First to win a goose keeps the goose.
Lanterns, painted, for the walk home.
Roast chestnuts in a bucket of hot embers.
Barley-sugar twists, sticky and criminal.
Hot broth for the guard on shift. Pay what you can.
Ribbon-braiders at work. A plait costs a song.
Honeyed nuts, a pinch of salt, a pinch of luck.
Pewter charms: a cup, a coin, a crooked little sword.
The smith's stall - horseshoes, thumb-rings, a very small knife.
Lamp-oil, wicks, and a pack of cheap cards.
Bone dice and a table. The house is honest. Mostly.
A bakery of sticky buns, steaming under cloth.
Plums in a jar, sugared, from a cellar nobody names.
A potion stall that swears it only sells cordial.
Meat pasties wrapped in cloth, still hot from the oven.
Mulled apples for the cold-fingered.
Garlands of straw and wild flower, three for a copper.
The apothecary's penny tonic - for headaches tomorrow.

notables.line: Agnes: 'Tonight the tab is on the house. Tomorrow the tab is on you.'
Agnes pours with both hands and counts with neither.
Agnes: 'Cups back by midnight. I know who took the last ones.'
Tobyn: 'No hammers tonight. Pretty near killed me to say it.'
Tobyn stands his anvil on the green as a table and no one has the nerve to mention it.
Tobyn: 'A good fire and a good crowd. That's nearly forge weather.'
Maud: 'The trout is fresh. The jokes are not. Take either.'
Maud sells the last fish and the first story of the night.
Bram: 'This barrel was meant for winter. Winter can find its own.'
Bram gives a toast, drinks it, and gives another.
Nell: 'If it's sweet and warm it's mine. Line up.'
Nell hands out cakes faster than the oven can answer.
Elspeth blesses the feast in under a minute, as promised.
Elspeth: 'Be glad. The gods have seen worse nights and survived them.'
Wat: 'Quiet job, this. Nice to see the living look lively.'
Wat toasts the ones he has dug a bed for, and lingers a moment.
Sibyl: 'Drink what you like. I have remedies for what you do not remember.'
Sibyl hands out cordial and a very small warning.
Godric: 'Stand easy tonight. Easy, not slack.'
Godric keeps one eye on the road and one on the pie.
Hob: 'Reed wreaths, fresh cut. For luck, or for hats.'
Hob has never danced. Tonight he stands very near the music.
Agnes sings the first line of the Ford song and then lets the room finish it.
Tobyn, flushed and happy, lifts a child up to touch the lantern.

e3po: E3PO attends the feast in full harness and declines a chair.
'Enjoy it. I will count the doors.'
The Commander allows himself exactly one cup. He holds it for an hour.
E3PO walks the edge of the green while the town dances.
'Festival is a lull, not a lie. The wall stays manned.'
E3PO nods at a drunk guardsman and takes his post for him.
The children climb the Commander like a siege tower. He holds still.
'Revel. Someone has to be sober for you.'
E3PO inspects the pies and finds them in good order.
The Commander hangs a lantern on the barracks door himself.
'No raid tonight. I would know. I check every hour.'
E3PO is asked to dance. He asks for a drill instead.
E3PO taps his helm to the fiddler. It is the highest praise he has.
'The town is happy. This is what the wall is for.'
A child puts a flower in the Commander's gauntlet. He tucks it in his belt.
E3PO raises his cup to the dark, in case it is listening.
'Cakes are good. Posture is better.'
The Commander sits, briefly, on the barracks step, and watches the green.
E3PO assigns four guards to the feast and eight to the gates.
'Do not pull the lanterns down. They make good beacons.'
E3PO declines to name the age of the cheese he is eating.
The Commander knows every dancer by name and corrects none.
'Laugh louder. It carries. The enemy likes to hear it fail.'
E3PO stands before the feast like a statue that has been told it can smile.
The Commander's helm has a ribbon on it. No one saw who put it there.
E3PO sips his ale as if it were a duty. He seems to enjoy the duty.
'I have never lost a feast, either.'
E3PO hums the Ford song under his breath, off-key, and stops when noticed.
The Commander is stopped three times on his round for a toast. He accepts all three.
'Eat well. Tomorrow the walls need you.'
closings: The lanterns gutter. Bellmire goes home full.
The fiddler lays down the bow. The green is quiet.
The last barrel is dry. The last song is not.
Bellmire sleeps it off. E3PO does not.
The tables are stacked, the ribbons gathered. Dawn will want them.
The crier rings once more. Feast over, town fed.
Pie crumbs, ribbon ends, one lost boot. A good night.
The embers go grey. The bell keeps the quiet.
The children are asleep in a heap beneath the long table.
A last toast, whispered, and the lanterns come down.
The fiddler and the dog walk home together.
The green is trampled flat and smiling.
Dawn finds the stalls folded and the guard sharp-eyed.
The feast ends the way all Bellmire things do: with someone sweeping.
'Same again next year,' says the crier, and means 'sooner'.
The last cup is raised to the dark. The dark does not answer.
A lantern left burning on the green. Nobody will say who for.
Bellmire is tired, and it is the good kind.
The feast ends. The wall's lamps burn on.
The hearth gets the last of the wood and the last of the stories.
The fiddles go back in their cases. The green goes back to being a green.
The guard changes. The party goes quietly home beneath them.
The bell tolls once to say 'night.' It says it kindly.
Home, feet sore, belly warm. The scar can wait till morning.

viewer_paid._note: A festival a VIEWER paid for. Richer than the ordinary set and every string may carry {buyer} - the paying viewer's display name. Cost statement: the buyer spends their bits/points to call it; the town celebrates for the festival's duration, and the lines credit the buyer by name. No guarantee of any other effect. No floor counts.
openings: {buyer} has paid for a feast. The crier has been told to be loud about it.
By {buyer}'s coin, Bellmire feasts tonight. Tables out!
{buyer} stands the whole town a festival. Nobody argues.
The guild treasurer reads the name aloud: {buyer}. A feast is called.
A festival, courtesy of {buyer}. The innkeeper has stopped counting.
{buyer} wants the lanterns lit. The lanterns are lit.
Bellmire owes {buyer} a feast, and is paying it forward as a song.
{buyer} paid, the barrel was tapped, and the green filled.
On {buyer}'s say-so, the long tables come out and the fiddlers tune.
The bell rings thrice for {buyer}. That means a feast.
{buyer} has bought the town a night off. The wall can wait.
Word from {buyer} reaches the Ford: Feast! The town hears it all at once.
A toast to {buyer}, who bought the ale and the music both.
{buyer} bought Bellmire a good night and it shows already.
Not a coin spent by the town tonight. {buyer} has covered it all.
The crier hoists a banner: 'Feast of {buyer}'.
Ribbons are cut in {buyer}'s name. The festival is on.
{buyer}'s gift becomes a festival. Even the geese are excited.
The innkeeper chalks {buyer}'s name above the door: 'Paid in full.'
{buyer} lit the fuse; Bellmire brought the powder. Festival!
A feast of {buyer}'s making. The town only has to show up.
The guild hall rings with {buyer}'s name and a good deal of clatter.
The crier practised {buyer}'s name all morning. Tonight he gets to say it.
{buyer} has called a festival and Bellmire does not dither.
crowd: Three cheers for {buyer}!
Who is {buyer}? Whoever they are, they're a saint!
Here's to {buyer} - and pass the pie!
{buyer}! {buyer}! {buyer}!
Somebody write {buyer} on the long table in flour.
I'd carry {buyer} home on my shoulders if I could find them!
A cup for {buyer}! A cup for the cup!
Is {buyer} here? Somebody find them and give them a cake!
Bless {buyer}'s open hands!
The brewer wants to meet {buyer}. For no reason. Except gratitude.
{buyer} bought the ale and the ale is good!
{buyer} the generous!
I'd march into the scar for {buyer} - after the cake.
Tell {buyer} the whole green says thank you!
Look - {buyer}'s ribbon is on the maypole!
Name a lantern for {buyer}!
The fiddlers know a song for {buyer} - it's the same song, but louder!
A kiss for whoever brought {buyer} to Bellmire!
They say {buyer} can hear us from beyond the Ford!
Say it again: {buyer}!
toasts: To {buyer}, who bought a night we won't forget!
To {buyer}: may your own table never be bare!
To {buyer}, and the good they send into the dark!
To {buyer} - Bellmire's friend beyond the Ford!
To {buyer}'s open hand, and the ale it poured!
To {buyer}, the patron of this evening!
To {buyer}: first cup is theirs, and so is the last!
To {buyer}, and may the road meet them kindly!
To {buyer}, the only guild we love more than our own!
To {buyer}'s name, now on the oldest wall we have!
To {buyer}: gold of the heart!
To {buyer}, whom the bell calls friend!
To {buyer}, who looked at Bellmire and said 'feast'.
To {buyer}'s health, wealth, and many a pie!
To {buyer} - may your luck run longer than our tabs!
To {buyer}, the reason for the crowd!
stalls: A cake iced with {buyer}'s name, wobbling slightly.
Mulled cider labelled 'The {buyer}' - warm and a little unwise.
Roast goose: 'by {buyer}'s leave', and nobody argues.
A honey-cake stall under {buyer}'s banner. Sold out in four minutes.
Free cups, tonight, thanks to {buyer}. Limit: all of them.
Painted lanterns, each with a small 'for {buyer}'.
Ribbon sellers have run out of {buyer}-coloured ribbon.
A sweet stall named in {buyer}'s honour: sticky, golden, famous.
The brewer's best barrel, tapped for {buyer}.
Pies marked with a crooked B, for 'buyer' - the baker's joke.
A lucky dip: every prize has {buyer}'s name on it, even the turnip.
A mulled-wine stall pours the first cup upright for {buyer}.
e3po: E3PO raises his cup to {buyer}, once, and drinks it like an order.
'To {buyer}. The wall is grateful. So am I.'
The Commander posts a guard of honour at {buyer}'s banner.
E3PO reports to the crowd: 'Our patron tonight is {buyer}.' The crowd roars.
'I do not drink to many. I drink to {buyer}.'
E3PO salutes the empty air beyond the Ford, where {buyer} might be listening.
'{buyer} is welcome at my gate, any hour.'
The Commander allows a second cup. For {buyer}.
E3PO lifts a child up to see {buyer}'s banner and holds still for a very long time.
'The wall does not bow. But tonight it nods, {buyer}.'
E3PO personally unrolls the banner that says {buyer}.
'Patrons like {buyer} are why a gate stays shut.'
E3PO says one dry word of thanks to {buyer} and means ten.
The Commander's helm has {buyer}'s ribbon on it. He wears it into the night.
'To {buyer}. May the road rise to meet them - and be dry.'
E3PO stands guard over the {buyer} barrel. No one steals from the patron.

notables.line: Agnes: '{buyer} paid for tonight. I only charge them for the next round.'
Tobyn: 'I'd forge {buyer} a medal if I knew what they'd done. Oh. That's it.'
Maud: 'Fish for {buyer}, free as water. Take two.'
Bram toasts {buyer} with the barrel itself.
Nell bakes a cake with {buyer}'s name on it and then eats a corner.
Elspeth blesses {buyer} by name, in a voice the whole green can hear.
Wat: 'Whoever {buyer} is, they bought a better night than I have ever had.'
Sibyl: 'A toast to {buyer}. May their cups be full and their mornings kind.'
Godric salutes {buyer}'s banner with a spoon.
Hob weaves a reed wreath for {buyer} and sets it on the banner.
Agnes carves {buyer}'s name into the bar with a hot nail.
Tobyn: 'Say what you like about heroes. {buyer} pays for the music.'

closings: The feast ends. {buyer}'s banner stays up till morning.
Bellmire drinks a last cup to {buyer} and goes home.
The crier calls it: 'Thank {buyer}, and goodnight.'
The fiddlers play {buyer}'s song once more, softly.
The last toast belongs to {buyer}. Everyone remembers.
The lanterns are left lit for {buyer}'s sake.
The festival folds. {buyer}'s name stays on the lips of the sleepy.
The innkeeper wipes the bar, then wipes {buyer}'s name off the board - reluctantly.
The town sleeps well, thanks to {buyer}.
The banner of {buyer} is folded and kept in the guild chest.
'Same again,' says the crier. 'If {buyer} pays.'
A final cheer for {buyer} - and the green falls quiet.
The guard changes. E3PO tips his helm to the empty air, for {buyer}.
{buyer} bought the night. Bellmire gives it back in memory.
The ribbons come down. {buyer}'s stays on the maypole.
A sleepy child asks the crier who {buyer} is. 'A friend,' says the crier.
stalls_alt: A pastry stall flies {buyer}'s name on a paper flag, and the flag is eaten by noon.
Spiced pears, roasted on the coals, a copper each - 'a copper for {buyer}', says the sign.
The ropewalk braids a ribbon in {buyer}'s colours and sells it by the yard.
A barrel of plums, free by {buyer}'s hand. The barrel is empty before the toasts.
The tinker rings a small bell every time somebody says {buyer}'s name. He is tired.
Hot chestnuts in paper twists: 'For {buyer}, while they last.' They do not last.
The dyer hangs a cloth in {buyer}'s favourite colour, whatever it was, and nobody checks.
A pie stall chalks 'BUYER'S SHARE' on the board and gives it away by the slice.
Warm bread, still steaming, handed over the stall with {buyer}'s name.
A spit of lamb turns slowly in {buyer}'s honour. The line is the length of the green.

notables_alt.line: Agnes: '{buyer} paid for the lamps. The least I can do is light them.'
Tobyn strikes a bell on the anvil, once, for {buyer}.
Maud: 'A basket of the best, for {buyer}. I picked them out myself.'
Bram: 'Whoever {buyer} is, the cellar is open. Do not tell my wife.'
Nell ices a loaf with {buyer}'s name and hands it to the first child she sees.
Elspeth rings the chapel bell once, for {buyer}, and says nothing else.
Wat clears the mud off the green with a broom, for {buyer}. It is not a small job.
Sibyl: 'To {buyer}. Whatever they spent, the town got more of it.'
Godric rows the ferry across for nothing, and says it is for {buyer}.
Hob stacks the cut reeds in a neat bundle at {buyer}'s banner and goes back to work.

viewer_paid._note_c120: C-120: stalls_alt (10) and notables_alt (10), same shapes and {buyer} placeholder as stalls and notables, which are untouched. Pick from the original plus _alt pool. No guarantee of any other effect. Additive; dead until wired.

phase2_words._note: THE WORDS PHASE 2 NEEDS (C-60, WORK_PLAN C2): the ascent (D77), the errand (D78), carry weight (D80), selling and the Guild vault (D81), the teleportation stone (D79), the upgrade poll (D66). Plain register - terse, nobody dramatic. Tokens in braces are filled by the game: {name} hero, {item} goods, {building} the building walked to, {shop} the shop, {hall} the Adventurer Hall, {floor} a floor the party stood on (never a floor total), {n} a number, {m} a capacity, {w} a weight, {v} vault contents, {who} a paying viewer. Where wear matters the pool is keyed by town band: patched (levels 1-4), mended (5-8), prosperous (9-12), the same twelve levels as shop_stock, trader_cargo, stock_by_tier and growth_tiers. Condition is the receipt for what viewers paid for: a legendary is never second-hand. Additive; dead until wired.

turn_around: We have what we came for. Turn round.
The flasks say go. We go.
Nobody is dying for one more room. Up.
{name} counts the flasks and turns for the stairs.
Enough. The way out is the way we came.
The party turns round on floor {floor}. It is a long way up.
Nothing carries them out. They walk.
climbing: Back up through floor {floor}. The same room, quieter.
Floor {floor}. They know it. It knows them.
Up a floor. The torches they left are out.
The door they broke is still broken. Something has been through it since.
They climb with the lamps low and the packs heavy.
The cleared floor is not empty. It never is.
Something has moved in behind them.
Whatever they left behind has started to come back.
repopulated: Rats in the cleared hall. Only rats, for now.
Something has been at the dead. Not the dead.
The scavengers found the floor first.
Gnawed bones where the fight was. Small teeth.
The scar closed a little behind them. Not all the way.
Nothing the size of a lord. Only what picks over leavings.
Carrion things have come to eat what the party left.
The blood is gone. Somebody licked the floor clean.
A few, and they wait by the stairs.
stairs_up: The stairs up are across the floor. The party walks to them.
{name} sees the stair. Open floor between.
The stair is where they left it. Nothing else is.
The way up is past the room they bled in.
spent: The flasks are low. The stairs are far.
Last flask. Nobody has drunk it yet. Someone is counting.
They spent everything getting down. Going up is the bill.
The satchel is nearly empty. The way up is not.
Going down was the cheap half.
out: {name} comes up out of the scar into daylight. The haul comes with.
Back through the gate. Alive, and carrying.
The party walks out of the scar. The guild writes the number down.
The air up here smells of bread. Nobody says anything about it.
chronicle_reached: Reached floor {floor}. Did not come up.
chronicle_came_back: Walked out from floor {floor}, and counted the flasks on the way.
wipe: Fell on the climb, on floor {floor}. The haul stays where they fell.
Died going up. What they carried is down there with them.
The haul is lost. It never reached the town.
They had it in their hands and not out of the door.
Nearly home. The guild records the floor they fell on.
A wipe on the climb is a wipe. Nothing comes home.

placed: {name} has an order in at {building}: {item}. Gold held.
Order placed: {item}, at {building}. {name} will go and fetch it.
{name} pays down on {item}. The {building} has it on a slip.
Bought is not carried. {name} has to walk it home.
{item} is promised at {building}. The slip is in {name}'s pocket.
walking: {name} crosses town to {building}. An order is waiting.
The {building} is not the market. {name} knows the way.
{name} goes for {item}. The walk is part of the price.

patched: {item}, handed over a plank counter. {name} pays what was held.
The {building} hands over {item}. The counter is a door on two barrels.
{item} comes out of a cupboard, patched in places. {name} signs with a thumb.
mended: {name} collects {item} at {building}. Counted out, signed for.
Wrapped in oilcloth. The {building} keeps a ledger now.
{item} comes off a shelf and into {name}'s hands. Everything on it is straight.
{name} collects {item}. The {building} has a stool for waiting now.
prosperous: {name} collects {item} at {building}. Boxed, and the box is good oak.
The {building}'s clerk reads out the price. {name} signs.
A proper counter, a proper receipt. {name} walks out with {item}.
Brass scale, clean ledger, and {item} laid on green cloth.
Wrapped in felt and handed across. {item} is {name}'s.

refused_level: The {building} does not stock that yet. Nothing taken, nothing held.
Too fine for this shop. Come back when the town is bigger.
{building} says no. {item} is above what it keeps.
A shop this size does not carry such things, and says so.
level_changed: The {building} grew while {name} was away. The order stays as placed.
{item}, as ordered. Nothing finer, though the shelves are fuller now.
interrupted: {name} was turned back on the way to {building}. The order stands.
The order waits. The {building} does not give it away.
waits_below: {name} is below. The order waits at {building} for the climb out.
An order sits at {building} for {name}, who is still down the scar.
{item} will be ready when {name} walks out. Gold is held; nothing else moves.
no_order: {name} came home with gold and bought nothing. Wears what they wore.
Gold in the purse, same kit on the back. {name} has not ordered.
A full purse is not a new sword. {name} has to go and ask for one.
gold_held: {n} gold held against {item}. It cannot buy anything else.
That gold is spoken for. {name} has an order out.
Purse light by {n}. The gold is at {building}, waiting for the slip.

encumbered: {name} walks heavier. The pack is winning.
Everything {name} owns is on their back, and it shows.
heavily_encumbered: {name} can barely walk. Every swing costs.
{name} is bent under it, a hand to the wall at every step.
Too much on {name}. They fight badly and know it.
pickup: {name} picks up {item}. It goes in the pack, and into the weight.
{name} takes {item}. Heavier by what it weighs.
over_capacity: Over what the party can lift. The stairs are steep.
Too much for the climb. Something has to stay.
They stand at the stairs and count what they can lift.
left_behind: {name} leaves {item} on floor {floor}. Cheapest by the pound.
{item} stays on floor {floor}. It was worth less than it weighed.
Left on floor {floor}: {item}. Someone will be sorry.
{name} sets {item} down on floor {floor} and does not look back.
dropped_stays: {item} lies where {name} set it down, on floor {floor}.
Still there. Nobody else is going to carry it.
come_back: The party turns round for what it left. The floor has changed.
greed: Strip a floor bare and you climb out under it.
Take what you can carry, not what you can lift.
A full pack is a slow way home.

placed: {name} takes {item} to the {shop}. A sale is an errand too.
sold: {shop} takes {item} for {n}. It will ask more for it.
{name} sells {item} for {n}. Less than it cost. It always is.
refused_level: A shop this size cannot buy {item}. It could not pay for it.
Too fine for this counter. {name} takes {item} home again.
The {shop} will not take a piece this good. It is not big enough yet.
A small shop cannot buy a legendary piece. That is a small town's whole trouble.
worn_below: {name} is below with it on their back. It cannot be sold from under them.
Worn in the scar. Not for sale until it comes up.

deposit: {name} puts {item} in the Guild vault at the {hall}. It weighs nothing there.
In the vault: {item}. {name} can carry on without it.
{name} walks {item} to the {hall}. The clerk logs it.
withdraw: {name} fetches {item} from the vault.
{item} out of the vault and onto {name}'s back. The weight comes back with it.
full: The vault is full. The {hall} has no more room.
No slot free. The {hall} is not big enough yet.
Every shelf is taken. A bigger Hall would have more.
raised: The {hall} grew. The vault has more shelves.
A new rack in the vault, and {who} paid for it.
death_kept: {name} is dead. What they carried is gone. What they stored is kept.
The vault keeps what the dead put in it. The next hero can use it.
Everything on {name}'s back stayed in the scar. The vault is untouched.
inventory: Pack {n} of {m}. Carrying {w}. The vault holds {v}.

bought: {name} bought a teleportation stone before going down. One stone, one hero.
{name} carries a stone. Panic, in a pouch.
A stone against the dark, bought before the gamble.
shatters: The stone shatters where {name} stands. {name} is gone from the floor and home in a breath.
{name} cracks the stone. The air folds. {name} stands in the square, shaking.
The stone breaks underfoot. The floor has one hero fewer.
one_hero: One stone, one hero. The rest of the party stays.
Nobody goes with {name}. The stone takes one.
lords_floor: The stone is dead weight here. A lord holds this floor.
Nothing happens. The lord is alive and the stone knows it.
{name} cracks the stone. It does nothing. The lord's floor will not let go.
Not on this floor. Not while the lord lives.
panic: One click, right now. That is what the stone is for.
The stone is the one thing a viewer can do this second.

opens: The town is asking. What should Bellmire build next?
A poll opens at the crier's post. The town can raise one thing.
The crier names the choices and the window they stay open.
rules: Channel points count as votes. Bits are added by the town's own count.
Cheers and power-ups cast in the window add weight. The tally is posted.
The rules are read out first: what counts, and when it closes.
closes: {building} will be raised. The masons are told.
credit: Raised by {who} and others. The Chronicle writes the names.
plaque: Lifted this season by {who} and the Hall's regulars.
shows: A new level on the {building}: a bigger front, a lit window, new stock.
The scaffolds come down. The {building} is bigger.
New stock on the shelf at the {building}.
ceiling: A level 1 shop cannot sell the best. Someone has to pay to raise it.
The ceiling is raised. The shop can stock finer now.

miniboss_feed._note: C-62 + C-67 second pool. Miniboss feed lines, one block per art-lane miniboss key (fourteen). Written under the permission that minibosses need no lore entry; these are feed lines only. Phases: arrive (set piece announced), act (the signature mechanic fires), broken (the weakness is hit and the mechanic stops), fall (death). Pick one line per event at random. {name} is a hero and may be absent from the choice of lines - substitute only where present. The game build wires them; nothing here changes a mechanic.
miniboss_feed._note_c74: C-74: +3 arrive and +4 fall on each of the fourteen minibosses (98 lines). Only arrive and fall are read by the game today (delve.gd _miniboss_say at spawn and at death), so those two pools were the ones repeating on stream; act and broken are not wired and were left alone. Same shapes; no mechanic changes. {name} not used in these lines.

arrive: Someone is beating the muster.
The gong is struck once. Somewhere a door opens.
A man in a dun coat stands in the barracks, mallet up.
The barracks door is open and the hall is full.
He walks the line. Nobody in it moves.
Dust in the barracks, and a row of beds made square.
The roll is called in the dark. Every name is answered.
A mallet on a gong, kept in time.
One blow on the gong, and the beds empty.
act: The gong again. The garrison falls in.
Boots on stone. More of them than before.
He calls the muster, and they answer.
Three short blows on the gong. Three more men.
The line stands a rank deeper.
"Fall in." They do.
A second file comes through the door.
broken: The gong is cracked. Nobody falls in.
The mallet drops. The drill is over.
The mallet is gone. The gong just hangs there.
Nobody answers the call.
fall: Karvok is down. The barracks is quiet.
No more muster. The gong hangs still.
Karvok is down. The line breaks and goes home.
Dismissed.
Karvok is down. The roll goes uncalled.
No more orders in this hall. The garrison does not get up.
The mallet lies where it dropped. The gong is still.
He drilled them well. It was not enough today.

arrive: It is wearing the workshop.
Plate on plate on an old dark core. It is not done yet.
Something is bolted together out of everything on the floor.
The bench is empty. Everything that was on it is walking.
It is the size of the cart it was built from.
Hammering, and the sound of something being fitted.
A bench of spares, and one thing that is not a spare.
It has been collecting for a long while. Today it is the whole collection.
The hammering stops. Whatever it was building is standing.
act: A plate comes off. It takes another from the floor.
It reaches down and mends itself.
The shell is thicker than it was.
A new plate, hammered on while it fights.
It takes a hinge off the wall and wears it.
Mended. Harder to hit than a minute ago.
Another layer. Same hands, same bolts.
broken: The floor is bare. It has nothing left to wear.
Down to the core, and nothing to put on.
The last plate rings off. What is under it is soft.
Stripped. It looks for more scrap and finds none.
fall: Ironhyde comes apart where it stands.
Scrap, all of it. The workshop keeps the pieces.
Ironhyde is down. The bench has its tools back.
A heap of old iron. Someone will sell it.
Ironhyde is down. The plates lie where they landed.
Nothing holds it together now. The bolts roll under the bench.
A rattle, then quiet. Someone will pick the good iron out.
It mended itself right up to the end.

arrive: A chain is paying out in the dark.
Iron on stone. Something is checking the cells.
Shacklemaw keeps the door and has not been relieved.
Keys on a ring, counted over and over.
Someone is working down the row of cells, slow.
A lantern, a hook, and a man who has never been late.
A cell door shuts somewhere, slow and certain.
The lamp is turned low. Shacklemaw likes it so.
A ring of keys, and a man who knows each one by feel.
act: The hook takes {name} out of the line.
{name} is dragged in on the chain.
One of the file is gone. The chain is short.
The hook finds {name} and the line is one short.
{name} is hauled out of the file by the collar.
Hooked. Nobody saw it thrown.
The chain runs out and comes back with someone on it.
broken: The hook is off its chain. Nobody else gets reeled in.
The chain goes slack.
The hook snaps. The chain is only chain.
He has nothing left to catch you with.
fall: Shacklemaw is down. The keys are still warm.
The chain lies where it fell. The cells are open.
Shacklemaw is down. The ring of keys goes quiet.
The cell door stands open. Nobody is sorry.
Shacklemaw is down. Every door on the row hangs open.
The keys slide off the ring. Nobody stops them.
Shacklemaw is down. The hook hangs off its chain.
The row is unwatched for the first time in years.

arrive: The nearest lamp has gone out.
A tall shape moves between the lamps.
Soot, and dead wax, and no light on the far wall.
The far lamp is dark and nobody put it out.
A long pole with a cup on the end.
Smoke, going the wrong way.
The lamps nearest the door are out. They were lit an hour ago.
A pole with a cup on the end, leaning in the doorway.
Cold wax, and a smell like a blown-out candle.
act: Another lamp out. The room is smaller.
Duskhollow takes the next light.
Fewer lamps. Closer shadows.
The pole comes down. Another wick is dead.
It does not hurry. It does not need to.
Two lamps left. Then one.
The dark takes another step in.
broken: The lamp stays lit. It has to take the next one.
Someone relights the wick. Duskhollow turns.
A wick catches. Duskhollow shies from it.
Lamp relit. The pole is slow now.
fall: Duskhollow is down. One lamp is still burning.
Dark, then a spark. Someone has a flint.
Duskhollow is down. Someone lights a lamp, and keeps hold of it.
Light on every wall. It was never a lot to ask.
Duskhollow is down. The pole rolls out of its hand.
A wick catches again, low and blue, then yellow.
It put out a good many lamps. Light them again.
Dark, then a match. The first light in the room is yours.

arrive: A spade is working somewhere in the dark.
Lit niches on a man's back. Count them.
Gravrik carries his own graves.
A bell tolls once for no one yet.
Fresh earth on the floor, and a spade in it.
Gravrik has dug for all of you already.
Spade-marks in the floor, and a heap of earth beside each.
A knell for someone not yet dead.
The niches along the wall are lit. A man in black is counting them.
act: A niche goes dark. The dead stand up.
The spade turns earth that is not there.
One more risen. One fewer lit.
A lamp goes dark. A grave opens.
The dead get up, one for every niche he put out.
The spade lifts and the floor gives one up.
Another stands. It was somebody once.
broken: The niches are empty. There is nothing left to raise.
Every grave open and nothing in them.
The last niche goes dark and nothing answers it.
He has no one left to call.
fall: Gravrik is down and stays down.
Back in the ground. He knows the way.
Gravrik is down. Somebody should dig for him.
Laid in his own work. Nobody will say a word over it.
Gravrik is down. His spade stays in the earth.
Gravrik is down. Nobody will ring for him.
The niches go out one by one. The dead stay down.
Spade down, bell still. Gravrik's work is done.

arrive: A bar has dropped behind you.
The leaf is across the door. Drudgewall is in front of it.
Oak and greased iron, and a man under them.
Hinges, and a very large man behind them.
The way out is somewhere behind that door.
Drudgewall sets his feet.
The big door is shut, and a big man is leaning on it.
A bar as thick as a man's leg, and a man who carries it.
Nobody has come through this door unasked. Nobody is asked.
act: The drawbar goes into the brackets.
Nobody leaves. Nobody comes in.
The door is shut. Fight the one in front.
The bar thuds home. The room is a room.
Nobody gets by. Nobody ever has.
He leans on the leaf and it holds.
broken: The bar is knocked out. The door is only a door.
The leaf is off its hinge. The way is open.
The bar splits. The door swings.
The leaf is off its pin. Go.
fall: Drudgewall is down. The bar comes up.
He kept the door. It is open now.
Drudgewall is down. The door stands open.
Unbarred. It was heavy work, and he did it.
Drudgewall is down. The door is just a door.
He held it as long as it needed holding.
The bar rolls off the brackets and clangs on the flags.
Drudgewall is down. His keys stay on his belt.

arrive: Something is counting what you carry.
A frame hung with other people's kit.
Velmok keeps a very good ledger.
A slate, a nail, and a tally cut in the wall.
It knows what each of you owes.
Chalk marks on a frame, and a good many of them new.
Slate, nail and chalk. Someone is adding up.
The frame is hung with other people's boots.
A neat hand in the margin. It has your names.
act: {name}'s kit comes off and goes on the frame.
It takes one thing and steps back toward the exit.
Another piece strung up. It is not done.
It takes {name}'s belt and hangs it up.
One more thing off the party and onto the frame.
It marks the tally and steps back.
A glove, a flask, a knife. All on the frame.
broken: The frame breaks. Everything it took hits the floor.
It lets go of the lot to save itself.
The frame cracks. The whole tally comes down.
What it stole spills across the floor.
fall: Velmok is down. Take your things back.
What it wore is on the floor. Count it twice.
Velmok is down. The tally is closed.
Get your things off the frame.
Velmok is down. The chalk breaks in his fingers.
The frame comes apart. Take back what was yours.
The tally is finished. Nobody owes.
The frame is bare by the time the dust settles.

arrive: The pot is on.
Steam, and the smell of a meal nobody asked for.
A yoke, a black pot, and a man who has been cooking a long time.
Someone has laid a table. It is not for you.
Fat in a pan and a smell you do not like.
Blisterhand is stirring. He does not look up.
Onions, and a fire banked high.
The pot is big enough to bathe in. It is not full of water.
A ladle taps the rim. Supper is on its way.
act: The pot rolls. The room is back on its feet.
Another ladle, and they are whole again.
The pack eats first.
A ladle of broth, and the wounded stand up.
He feeds the one in front first.
The pot steams. The pack looks better for it.
Hot food for hurt men. It works.
broken: The pot is spilled. The pack is only a pack.
Nothing hot left in it. Nothing left to heal.
The pot tips and the broth runs out across the floor.
Cold, and empty. He cannot mend them now.
fall: Blisterhand is down. The fire goes out.
Supper is cancelled.
Blisterhand is down. The pot is empty and so is he.
No more suppers. The fire dies back.
Blisterhand is down. The ladle rings on the floor.
The fire gutters. Nothing is left on it.
The pot goes cold. Nobody eats.
Blisterhand is down. The kitchen smells of smoke and nothing else.

arrive: The water is coming up.
A wheel turning somewhere, and the floor wet.
Rothenwell winds the gate a notch at a time.
The walls are dripping. They were dry a minute ago.
A great iron wheel, turning with no one on it.
He has been waiting for the river for a long time.
A gate is cranked open somewhere above.
The floor is wet, and the drip is getting faster.
A keeper at the wheel, and the channel behind him full.
act: Another notch. Water to the ankle.
The gate gives a little more. Knee-deep.
Higher. The wheel is still turning.
The wheel turns. The floor is wet to the shin.
More water. It is cold, and it is rising.
Another turn of the gate. Boots are heavy.
The channel fills. The room is a trough.
broken: The wheel is jammed. The water holds where it is.
The gate drops shut. The floor begins to drain.
The wheel stops. The water stops with it.
The gate falls shut and the water begins to run out.
fall: Rothenwell is down. The water goes out slow.
The wheel stops. So does the flood.
Rothenwell is down. The channels are drained, slowly.
Dry again, in time. Wring out your cloak.
Rothenwell is down. The gate sticks where it is.
The wheel runs backward and the water finds a drain.
Silence, and the sound of the channels emptying.
Rothenwell is down. The channel drains, and the stones steam.

arrive: Something is broadcasting seed.
Wherever it walks, the ground is a little greener.
Thorncast comes across the grass with a full hand.
Green shoots in a place nothing grows.
It walks the field the way a farmer walks his own.
A sack on its shoulder, and every step plants something.
Seed on the stone, and green in the cracks.
A hand in the sack, a hand on the ground.
The field does not belong here. Thorncast walks it anyway.
act: What it casts stands up as thorn.
The ground has teeth where it was bare.
Thorn where {name} was about to step.
It scatters a handful. The ground bristles.
Thorn, and then more thorn.
What it throws takes root before it lands.
{name} stands in a hedge that was not there.
broken: The seed bag is empty. The thorn stops coming.
Out of seed. It has only its hands.
The sack is slit and empty. No more thorn.
It scrapes the bottom of the bag. Nothing.
fall: Thorncast is down. The thorn will not last.
Nothing more planted. The field starts to go back.
Thorncast is down. The thorn begins to brown.
The field is only a field again.
Thorncast is down. The sack is empty and so is the field.
Nothing sprouts where it fell.
Thorncast is down. The thorn goes soft at the root.
Every stalk leans toward the body, then lies down.

arrive: The lines were here before you.
Cord at ankle height, set a long time ago.
Nothing in the wood is where it looks.
The wood is quiet and every branch is tied to another.
A loop of cord by the door. Another by the stair.
Griplash is somewhere near. You are standing on its lines.
Cord, knotted at the knee, strung from beam to beam.
A branch bent back and held. It is not holding itself.
The floor is clear. Every tile of it is a decision.
act: It herds the party onto its own lines.
A snare takes {name} at the ankle.
The room closes. Every step was chosen for you.
A line pulls tight. The party is pushed one way.
Cord at the ankle. {name} is down.
It does not chase. It lets the lines do it.
The room is smaller. All its doors are traps.
broken: The lines are cut. The room is only a room.
Cord in pieces. Griplash has nowhere to drive you.
The cord goes slack. The traps hang loose.
Cut one line and the whole set comes down.
fall: Griplash is down, caught in its own set.
Pull the lines up before anyone else walks them.
Griplash is down. Walk out the way you came, carefully.
Left in his own net. There is a kind of justice in it.
Griplash is down. The lines slacken all at once.
Walk soft. The loose cord still bites.
Griplash is down. Nothing in the room is waiting for your foot.
A last snap, and the set lies slack on the floor.

arrive: The pit has been fed.
Heat, and a shape as big as the fire it keeps.
Cindrak has not let the pit go out.
The heat comes before the man.
A shovel, a furnace door, and a very patient man.
Cindrak is feeding the fire. It is feeding him.
A furnace door standing open, and no one near it.
The coal-bunker is empty. The fire is not.
Heat first, then the sound of a shovel.
act: Another log in. It stands taller.
The fire climbs, and so does he.
Fed again. Hotter.
A shovel of coal and the pit roars.
He grows with every log.
The fire is up. So is he.
The furnace door swings open. Nobody wants that heat.
broken: The fuel is scattered. It is smaller already.
Starve the pit. It is the same size as the fire, and the fire is going.
The coal is kicked out. He shrinks with it.
The fire sinks. He is smaller than he was.
fall: Cindrak is down. The pit goes to ash.
Cold. First time in a long while.
Cindrak is down. The furnace is cold.
Nothing left to feed. It is quiet now.
Cindrak is down. The furnace ticks as it cools.
The fire goes out slowly. It took a lot to feed.
Cindrak is down. The shovel is too hot to lift.
Ash, a shovel, and the smell of a long shift ending.

arrive: A bell, and not where you thought.
Fog, and a note from the wrong side of the room.
Tolburn is in the fog, and the sound is somewhere else.
A bell tolls and you cannot say from where.
Fog on the floor, and a rope hanging in it.
Tolburn has been ringing since before you came in.
One note, and then the fog closes round it.
A bell-rope swings with nobody on it.
The bell sounds from all sides. He is on one of them.
act: The bell rings behind you. It is in front.
A stroke from the left. He is on the right.
The sound is a lie. Do not go toward it.
The bell rings. Half the party turns the wrong way.
A note from the left. Nobody is there.
He rings it behind {name}. It is not behind {name}.
The sound moves. He does not.
broken: The bell is cracked. It is only a man now.
One flat note, and it comes from where he stands.
The bell cracks. It rings flat and true.
One clean stroke, and you know where he is.
fall: Tolburn is down. The last note rings out and stops.
Silence in the fog. The right kind.
Tolburn is down. The bell swings once more and is still.
The fog thins. It is only a room.
Tolburn is down. The fog lifts off the floor.
No more bells. The echo takes a while to go.
The rope drops. The bell is only iron.
Tolburn is down. You know where everything is again.

arrive: Something is pouring.
Sugar and heat, and the smell of a kitchen with no cook.
Scaldmere stirs, and the floor is stickier than it was.
A kettle the size of a cart, and something stirring it.
The air is thick and sweet. Stay clear of the floor.
Scaldmere has been at the pan a good while.
Sugar scorching somewhere nearby.
The pan is bubbling. Nobody is watching it but him.
The floor sticks to your boots, and it is getting warmer.
act: It pours. The floor goes hard round {name}'s feet.
Set fast. Nobody is going anywhere.
Another pour, another stuck boot.
A ladle of syrup across the floor. It sets.
{name}'s boots are fast in it.
He pours again. The floor hardens round the party.
Sweet and hot. Then hard as horn.
broken: The pan is empty. Nothing left to set.
The pour stops. The floor cracks free.
The kettle is empty. The pour stops.
The pan cracks and runs dry.
fall: Scaldmere is down. The floor stays hard for a while.
Cooled and done. Chip your boots loose.
Scaldmere is down. The pan is cold.
Everything he poured is going to harden. Get free of it.
Scaldmere is down. The pan goes off the boil.
The last pour runs thin and cold.
Scaldmere is down. It smells like a fair after the stalls close.
The kettle tips and the sweet runs off the stone.

arrive: Someone has opened the armoury.
The barracks stores are open and a man is counting.
A ledger snaps shut. He has been waiting.
Racks emptied, and the stores book signed.
Keys on a ring, and the lock already turned.
Spears out of the rack, every one issued.
A man in a store coat, and a queue of things that bite.
Wardgrim has been through the stores.
Issue day. Nobody asked for it.
fall: Wardgrim is down. The stores are shut.
The ledger stays open at the last line.
Wardgrim is down. Nothing more to issue.
Keys on the floor. Nobody picks them up.
Wardgrim is down. The racks are bare.
Counted out, and signed for.
Wardgrim is down. The barracks is quiet again.
Issued the last of it. Nothing left on the shelf.

arrive: Something is hauling in the mess hall.
Crates stacked high, and a man under them.
A rope, a lamp, and a very large load.
Millstone is carrying more than he should.
Sacks, a keg, and boots too heavy to hurry.
The store-hands have left. He has not.
A lamp swings from a bundle the size of a cart.
He walks slow. He has a lot on his back.
Boots heavy on the boards, and the load comes in first.
fall: Millstone is down. The crates come with him.
Millstone is down. The load lies where it landed.
Rope slack, and the lamp on its side.
Millstone is down. Somebody will have to stack it again.
Sacks split on the floor. Grain everywhere.
Millstone is down. The keg rolls off alone.
Put it all down at last.
Millstone is down. It was a heavy day.

arrive: A hurdle goes up across the room.
Split grey hurdles. Stood out in the rain a long time.
A panel drops between you and the rest.
He pens the room like a meadow.
Stakes driven, and the line already cut.
A fence where there was no fence.
Bramblejaw has walked in. Somebody is on the wrong side.
Wattle and rope, and a man behind it.
Wattle creaks, and the room is in two halves.
fall: Bramblejaw is down. The hurdles lie flat.
A hurdle just went down between you.
Bramblejaw is down. The line is one line again.
Stakes pulled. The pen is open.
Bramblejaw is down. Step over the wattle.
Rope slack, and the gap closed.
Bramblejaw is down. Nobody is penned.
Rotten wattle, split through.

arrive: It is pinned together.
One pin holds it. Both halves are working.
A mallet on one side, a saw on the other. One body.
You can see through the middle of it.
Two lamps at two heights, and one pin between them.
It stands on two blocks and works with three arms.
The spare arm hangs on its peg. The other two are busy.
Sawdust on the floor, and a pin as thick as a wrist.
It is a joint that learned to walk.
fall: The pin is out. Both halves lie where they stood.
Halvrek is down. It does not come apart again.
Two halves, and neither one is moving.
The mallet rolls one way and the saw the other.
Halvrek is down. The pin is still in it.
Split down the seam. Someone will sell the timber.
It held together as long as the pin did.
The trestles are empty. Halvrek is done for the day.

arrive: It is pegging up a fresh hide.
Wet hides on every line. It is wearing the newest.
The pit smells of lime and old water. Something is working in it.
A stooped frame, and a skin still dripping.
It looks you over the way it looks over a hide.
Nothing down here is allowed to get old. It sees to that.
The tan-pit is occupied.
It has been soaking something for a week. It is done waiting.
It has dressed worse than you.
fall: Flenscar goes down in its own pit.
The hides come off the lines and into the water.
Flenscar is down. The pit stops smelling of work.
A last hide, half pegged. Nobody finishes it.
It had an answer for every blow but the last.
Down. The lime water takes the apron.
Flenscar is down. Its hands are still the colour of the pit.
The pegs are bare. Flenscar is done.

arrive: It is here for the lord's share.
A small man, a big box, and a chain between them.
It is counting what you have not carried yet.
It sits by the box with the ledger open.
The chain does not let it leave. It does not need to.
Everything on this floor is owed to somebody. It keeps the book.
A toll, and it has a face.
It has been here since the floor was laid. The rent is due.
The box is open. The count has started.
fall: Lockwarden is down. The box is yours.
The chain hangs loose. Nothing is pulling it.
The ledger is shut. The share stays where it is.
Lockwarden is down. Nobody is taking a cut today.
Quiet at the box. The count is whatever you say it is.
Down, still tied to the box it guarded.
Lockwarden is down. The lord's share is not coming for you.
The last tally is half written. Nobody finishes it.

arrive: Something in here is drinking.
A tun with the tap open, and a man standing over it.
It smells of the cellar. It is not offering.
The tap keeps running. Whatever you brought goes down it.
It has the look of a man who has never paid for a round.
A cask the size of a cart, and Dregsallow, who has not moved.
Whatever you brought, it has a mug for.
Keep your brews corked.
The tap is open and it is not for you.
fall: Dregsallow is down. The tun runs dry.
The tap drips, then stops.
Down. The cask rings empty.
Dregsallow is down. What is left is yours.
It poured the last one for itself.
Dregsallow goes over with the tap still open.
A last drip off the spigot. Then quiet.
Dregsallow is down. Nobody is serving.

arrive: It has a yoke, and it is looking for something to put in it.
Chains on the floor, collars on the chains. One is still warm.
It waits for the first one to fall.
The press stands open. It is hoping for company.
A flared coat and a yoke at the shoulder. It has done this before.
It does not hurry. Someone always goes down.
Four collars hang off it. They are not ornaments.
It was the prison's press. It kept the habit.
It collects the ones who fall. It is patient about it.
fall: Crushwright is down. The yoke comes off whoever it held.
Every collar drops open at once.
The chains go slack all down the floor.
Crushwright is down. Get your people up.
The yoke lies on the floor. Nobody is in it.
It could not hold them once it was down.
Crushwright is down. The collars lie empty.
A last clink, and the chains stop.

arrive: Something in here is taking the heap off.
A man with a scale and a straight stick. He means to level you.
He draws the stick across the rim. Whatever stood proud is gone.
A bushel is a bushel. He sees to it.
The beam hangs from a post at his side. He is waiting for the pans to settle.
He does not weigh anyone. He sets them to the measure of the worst.
The strongest in the file will feel it first.
A market officer's stick, and a market officer's patience.
He was the treasury's measure. He kept the habit.
fall: Murkspit is down. The stick slips out of his hand.
